title: Love the app, but missing two essential features.
body:
Love the app, but missing two essential features!

I really love Structured! It’s a great way to organize my daily to-dos and keep track of things I don’t necessarily want cluttering up my main calendars. It helps me stay focused on what I need to accomplish each day.

However, two missing features are incredibly frustrating: a full monthly calendar view and a search function. I’d love to be able to see everything I have planned at a glance without having to scroll through individual days. And not being able to search for a task or something I’ve scheduled makes it unnecessarily difficult to find things.

These two features would make a huge difference in usability and take an already great app to the next level. I really hope the developers consider adding them!

title: Paid for Lifetime, Disappointed by Missing Two-Way Calendar Sync
body:
Structured is a great app in many respects, and I paid for the lifetime subscription. However, the lack of two-way calendar sync is a major limitation for me. I need changes made in the app to update my calendar and vice versa.

That’s why I use the lifetime version of Planny, another German app, instead. For a paid planning app, seamless two-way calendar integration is something I consider essential. Disappointing that Structured still doesn’t offer it.

title: Make checking tasks off more visually appealing

It gives me an instant sense of accomplishment and makes me want to keep that streak going.

I think adding something similar, like confetti, fireworks, animations, or even customizable completion effects, would make checking off tasks so much more satisfying and motivating.

title: Amazing!
body:
I love this app in almost every way. The owners are incredibly responsive to App Store reviews, feedback, and any issues that come up. The level of detail throughout the app is amazing.

One of my favorite things is that you can genuinely use it without paying. And even if you do upgrade, there’s a one-time purchase option, which is incredibly refreshing compared to apps that lock everything behind another monthly subscription.

My only major suggestion: please, please gamify the platform more. As someone with severe ADHD who struggles with staying focused and consistent, I think a deeper points/rewards system could be a game changer. The existing energy system is a great start, but I’d love to see things like XP, levels, streaks, achievements, rewards, and even point penalties for missed goals.

Adding that extra layer of progression and dopamine would make self-improvement feel more like a game, something you actually want to keep coming back to every day. For someone like me, that could take an already great app to another level.

title: A Home Screen Mainstay
body:
I downloaded Structured a few years ago to see if it could help me manage my ADHD, and honestly wasn’t sure how much I’d actually use it. There are less than 10 apps that have changed my Home Screen layout, and this became one about 3 weeks after downloading it and hasn’t moved since. 

The Inbox is probably what made it click for me. I can just throw everything I need to remember in there (as it comes to me, not at once). Then, if I’m planning my day, I can actually give everything a place and dedicate time to focus on it, or just add things in as I go and set a time limit. It’s helped a ton with both forgetting things and having a million things I know I need to do but no idea where to start. Not to mention the focus timer screen and widgets! 

I was unsure about premium at first, but after using the app for a while I ended up going for it and it’s been worth it every day. The newer Structured AI feature has been especially great. My days obviously never go exactly according to plan, so being able to easily readjust everything when something takes longer or shorter than expected makes the difference of giving up vs calibrating my updated times.

Huge thanks to the people who build and maintain this app. It’s genuinely one of the few productivity apps that has stuck with me for years and actually made my life easier. Also, thank you for putting so much emphasis and effort into making it visually appealing because I definitely cannot focus on a productivity app if I hate looking at it 😂

Structured absolutely needs a search function. The premium version needs a way to prevent tons of duplicates from stacking on top of each other. Some pop-up asking if you meant to create a duplicate if the task already exists on a day would be nice. The AI in the premium version isn't very helpful. 

Structured has a checklist with a nice widget and some fun icons to make seeing the tasks easier at a glance.

It has some disadvantages that other apps, such as FlowSavvy, don't have. Some of those disadvantages are: Structured has no search function at all (not even in the premium version), overlapping tasks creating a visual mess (FlowSavvy stacks them next to each other if they overlap, instead of directly above/below as Structured does), and no repeating tasks unless you have premium (FlowSavvy lets you repeat tasks on the free version). 

The search function for Structured has been on their roadmap for almost 4 years. The allowance for overlapping tasks that don't disturb the task flow has been on the roadmap for almost 3 years and was rejected, with no clear reason given.

That said, Structured is quite reasonably priced and even has a lifetime purchase option.

title: I LOVE This App, but the Inbox Is HORRIBLY PAINFUL! Please end the suffering!
body:
I absolutely love this app except for one thing: The Inbox.

If it wasn’t for the inbox, I would give this app five stars. In fact, I would give it more if I could.

The Inbox is so painful to use on a tablet and especially on a phone if you have a lot of items sitting there that you haven’t scheduled yet. And isn’t that the whole point of an inbox? I put things there because I know I need to do them, I don’t want to forget them, but I don’t necessarily know yet when I’m going to do them.

I currently have around 20 things in my Inbox, and trying to organize them is incredibly frustrating. You have to press and hold each task and drag it where you want it. But if you’re trying to move something farther up the list, once you reach the top of the screen, IT DOESN’T KEEP SCROLLING. It just stops. So you have to let go of the task, scroll the list to make more room at the top, find the task again, drag it farther up, and keep repeating this process.

Why???

There’s also no way to filter or sort the Inbox by category, which would at least make managing a larger Inbox easier.

What frustrates me so much is that I genuinely LOVE this app. I have a lot of plates spinning in my life, with both big and little things I need to remember, and Structured is exactly the kind of app I need. But I’m starting to wonder if the Inbox is actually helping me manage all of those things or just giving me another frustrating list that I have to manage.

Please fix this user experience. At the very least, tasks should continuously scroll when you drag them to the top or bottom of the screen. Even better, give us ways to sort, filter, group, or otherwise organize the Inbox.

I design software, so I understand that development takes time and priorities have to be made. But this feels like such a fundamental usability issue in a core part of the app. Please make it a priority.

I really don’t want to stop using Structured because I love almost everything else about it. But the Inbox is making me want to.

title: Great for Nuerodivergents!
body:
I have had this app for three years and it truly had saved my life. I have ADHD and time blindness, so I struggle to visualize and estimate my time like normal people. With this, I am visually able to see all the time in my day, and it keeps me on track with alerts/notifications for the start and end of a task so I know when to wrap up.  

You can keep your to do list in it too, and drag and drop it into your schedule when you’re ready. My whole brain is in this. 

It really helped me when I was in college. When I had assignments and didn’t know when I’d be able to fit them in my schedule. And I would get alerts that I’d have an event that I probably forgot about. 

Then you just check everything off. And anything you didn’t get done in the day, you can just drag and drop it into tomorrow. 

I’ve tried a lot of different scheduling apps, and this one has been the best so far. 

Super user friendly, and they consistently update it, so it only gets better.

title: ADHD girlies, sign up now!
body:
I am fortunate to be an OG lifetime membership user. I believe I got the pro plan early on for something like $20. I have since converted at least a dozen of my close friends and family. This is a perfect app that only continues to grow, improve, and impress. I could not function without it and I could not recommend it enough!

The mobile version has reshaped how I can approach my days and my time management. There are so many wonderful features to help you balance your time and energy. It’s beautifully designed, the architecture is sound, the integration is already great and continues ro improve.

Eventually, I’m excited for the desktop version to grow - navigating this version has been a bit finicky (however I just got a new laptop and I’m excited to see if those issues were device specific). But I’m ultimately grateful for how well it syncs between devices and allows for aesthetic customization.

I have heard from friends who I recommended this to before that the price has gone up a bit - hopefully not too aggressively. But whatever the price, if its reasonable to you, this app is highly efficient and carries an undeniably positive impact on the lives of people who use it!

Enjoy!

title: Solved My Time Management Struggles!
body:
If you thrive on a schedule but need flexibility to fit your ever changing routine, this is the app for you! My plans are always changing, but I need routine and structure to survive, so I live off of this app. 

Pros:
- I use the free version and I only get the occasional pop up to try their paid version (I might get the pop up once or twice a day maybe).
- It’s very simple to move plans around and make new ones.
- It can connect to your health app and show you where you are in your cycle if you like to plan your day around that.
- It even has an energy tracker option where you can see how much energy your tasks take and plan your day around how much energy you have. 
- I love that I can plan my day as simple or in-depth as I’d like.
- Looks cute and is very customizable 
- I love that it’s compatible with my laptop and smart watch, so I always have an idea of how long my current task is and how long till my next task starts. 

Cons:
- literally none, this app is amazing!


If you need help with time management or making the most of your day, I 1,000% recommend this app!

title: Runs HOT & Drains battery like crazy
body:
So I really did use to love this app, so much so that I’ve been using the premium version for over a year now actually, however it’s no longer worth it unfortunately… 

Within the past few months anytime I open the app on my phone now it starts to drain my battery like crazy. I’m talking every 30 seconds I loose one percent battery at least! And that’s just if I have the app open. Once I start trying to actually time block too then my phone starts to get super glitchy & run extremely hot as well. So hot that only after a few min of using the app my phone will soon be burning my hands up & I’ll have to let it cool off before I can use it again. This is not normal! 

At first I thought maybe my phones battery was just starting to go bad since I’ll admit I may not have the newest iPhone on the market, & sure my battery isn’t as great as it once was, but this is in fact the only app that causes me problems & force closing this application is the only thing that instantly solves all those problems. Therefore it’s definitely not exclusively an issue with my battery, but rather within the app itself. 

Ultimately I’m not sure what bug randomly brought this on, but I suspect that if I do attempt to keep using this app then I really will start to have issues with my phones battery as no app should ever cause a phone to get that hot!
Especially a simple calendar app you’d think?

That said, sadly I’m left with no other choice than to cancel my yearly membership & delete this glitchy thing off my phone ASAP before it has the chance to do anymore damage. The only reason I haven’t deleted it yet is cuz I was hoping the next update would resolve these issues. Alas, multiple app updates later, including multiple phone updates later, & I’m still having problems so I simply can’t risk it anymore. Clearly this bug isn’t going away…

Initially, I was pretty excited about this. But the more I work with it, the more time I spend trying to figure out how to get the interface to put tasks where I need them to be on the calendar. It’s a bit of a mystery to me how the designer wanted this to work or how it was supposed to be. But in any case, it takes me about 3 to 4 times as long to put a task on a schedule compared with using something like Apple’s calendar.

I’ll keep on fiddling with it and perhaps I can raise my review. But it is an odd interface and I kind of wish I hadn’t paid the subscription.

I’m not always perfect, but when I slip, this app really helps me get back on track without guilt for missing an item or even a day. title: Transforming Time Management with Color, Clarity, and Compassion
body:
As a mental health coach, staying organized and engaged is essential for supporting my clients and managing my online presence. Structured has been a game-changer for me! The vibrant colors make planning enjoyable and keep me motivated throughout the day. I love how easy it is to track my time and daily activities, which helps me stay on top of client sessions, content creation, and online engagement.

I also love recommending Structured to clients with ADD/ADHD—the colorful, visual layout helps them stay engaged and better understand how their time is “structured”😉. One of the most valuable aspects is how it allows both me and my clients to realistically assess our schedules. By visually mapping out our days, we can identify when we might be setting unrealistic expectations for ourselves and make adjustments to ensure our plans are actually achievable in today’s fast-paced world.

I’m especially excited to explore the AI features to further streamline my workflow. Highly recommended for professionals and anyone looking to boost productivity, maintain a strong online presence, and approach time management with greater self-compassion and realism!

title: Habit tracking
body:
I really enjoy using this app. It has helped me learn and stay consistent, and the experience is smooth and motivating. However, I would love to see a habit tracking feature added in the future.

A habit tracker would help users monitor their daily progress, stay consistent, and build long-term routines. For example, tracking how many days in a row I practice, setting daily goals, and seeing progress statistics would be extremely helpful and motivating.

title: Best planner by far for ADHD brains
body:
I love the features of this planner. It is the closest to how I set up my bullet journal. Being able to replan tasks (and decide whether they are valuable anymore) or pop them to an inbox so I can clear them out of my metal clutter but not lose them entirely are excellent features.  I love the idea of “energy expenditure” as it forces me to really consider whether I will have the energy for something, not just the time.  If I run out of steam before finishing all my duties in a day, I can make a more realistic plan in the future, given energy constraints, rather than kicking myself for being “lazy.” So important for mental health AND for getting the work done. The UI is excellent.

I enter things into my Apple Calendar and then use Structured to check things off through the day, so I have noticed two items which might improve this further: I wish it could pull travel time from my Calendar, so that I don’t add tasks into space where I need to be driving; and it would be nice to be able to add an unexpected event or task (let’s say run to the grocery store for 30 mins) and have everything bump forward accordingly, rather than having to hand slide it to eliminate overlaps. If this were added, having some events able to be toggled as “locked” and un-bumpable would be important (for example, a class that happens at a certain time).

Otherwise, really outstanding planner.  Thoughtful updates and amazing attention to details that work well for ADHD brains!

title: Best app I’ve ever used
body:
I’ve only been using this app 3 days and I already love it! 

I’m starting to up there in age and am finding my present digital calendar a little overwhelming. Don’t get me wrong I still like Google’s calendar. Especially the fact you can invite people to events. We use it as a family calendar. 

But…. For my personal use I wasn’t finding it all that useful anymore. There is just too much information on it. Especially when using on my phone. 

Structure is different. The format is perfect for phone use. I can scroll easily from day to day and I get reminders on what’s coming up. It sinks with my family Google calendar, so I can keep up with what everyone else is doing. 

The best feature for me is the mailbox. I’m keeping my grocery list there. I created a grocery task and am keeping it the mailbox. It just sits there off to the side and I add items as they come up. If you add them as sub tasks it essentially creates a checklist. When I’m ready to go shopping I just add it to that days tasks and can check off my items as I shop. My daughter thought it was the cleverest thing ever.

title: Structured changed my life!
body:
I’ve been struggling with ADHD since childhood, and I’ve tried countless apps, systems, and productivity hacks to fix my planning and follow-through. Structured is easily the most helpful tool I’ve ever used. 

The AI feature is a game changer. It’s not 100% perfect but it’s so close and once you learn how to phrase things it becomes incredibly effective. When I’m busy or honestly just feeling stuck, I can basically ramble out what I need to get done or how my day has changed, and it can turn that into an organized plan with brakes. It genuinely starts to feel like having a real Assistant.

The syncing with my calendar and reminder is also extremely useful and saved me from double entering everything. I also love the energy level feature, it helps track how much effort different tasks take, which makes it easier to understand why some days still exhausting and how much I’ve actually accomplished.

That said, there are a couple areas that could improve. The documentation was hopeful, but it could be better organized, and easier to find, it didn’t seem like everything was available directly in the app, but instead on the website. Even on the website, it seemed disorganized and kind of hard to follow, which could’ve been solved with a better table of contents to feature maybe. I’ve also hit a few bug bugs like the Apple Watch app crashing when I tap certain buttons, even though notification still work reliably. There also been some strange error messages that appeared occasionally but nothing serious and I’m sure it’ll get corrected in the future.

Overall, even with a few rough edges, structured has made a bigger difference for me than any other app I’ve tried, and I genuinely recommend it, especially for anyone who struggles with planning, timelines, or executive function

title: REALLY Wish You Had These 2 Things!!!
body:
1. A way to organize and delete suggested tasks. Yes, I went on a generous number of dates with a person in this town. No, I do not want to be reminded of this terrible person with a task related to them when I am filling out my work schedule for the week. Others have said similar about being reminded of dead pets with suggested tasks related to them. I’m honestly shocked it isn’t possible to do this since it seems like an obvious human factor

2. PLEASE create a view mode similar to google calendar with visual BLOCKS of time, as well as the names of the tasks and the times scheduled for them!!! My ADHD just doesn’t get anything from circular icons dragging down my screen that forces me to look at it in another view mode I didn’t want in the first place just to see what the task even is. The google style would be absolutely amazing in month view, week view, and day view. Can’t say how many times I’ve heard other users comment on this lack of a good visual overview design. Seeing it in this way would make it so much easier for me to quickly see at a glance what I can fit into my schedule and what I can’t!

I love what this app has done for me so far (suggested tasks other than the mentioned issue is GREAT, the minimal yet colorful design is appealing) but until I see these 2 major improvements I will continue to look at alternatives.

title: Surgery recovery simplified!
body: I’m a regular user of Structured. I’m currently unemployed and have ADHD and I’m giving Structured credit for me finally adding, wait for it, structure, to my mornings. However, it was immensely helpful during my current nasal surgery recovery. I was prescribed an hourly saline spray in addition to meds. Day one of recovery I wrote out my schedule in my planner, took a pic and uploaded so the AI feature could do the work of getting it into the app for me. Day 2, I was super groggy, so I just voice to texted what I needed including “meds after lunch” and “meds after dinner”. Structured’s AI appropriately placed those items even without being given a specific time. The hours are going by SO fast that I KNOW I would have only done the spray a handful of times if it wasn’t for Structured’s reminders. Highly highly highly recommend this app. I feel like there used to be a “snooze” option a few years ago. I’d definitely use that feature if it was available.

body:

title: Go back to your roots
body: When I first downloaded this app, it was the most efficient way to plan a day. I pressed the plus, typed the task, it defaulted to a time, and automatically placed it right behind each previous task. I was able to quickly schedule my day in the most efficient way possible. Then somewhere along the way, the app decided to think for me. When I typed the first letter of a task, it auto filled, and defaulted to previous name, and time, that I had used the day before, or past history. This change meant I had to look at the last task I wanted to do in the new schedule and figure out the time that’s supposed to go behind it, because it wouldn’t automatically place it behind the last task scheduled. This change negated the simplicity that I so loved. I emailed the developers to see if there was a way to turn off history and that’s a no. This last update: I thought that might have been fixed, so I downloaded again hoping. I was saddened to see that instead of opening to the simple schedule KISS, it not opens to a weekly (very busy screen), schedule. Finally found that the simple blank screen I loved is able to be reached by pulling up at the bottom. The simplicity of this planner was scheduling by the day and autogrouping as many tasks as I could fit in, in an 8 hour period. If you’re wanting a weekly planner, this may be what you’re looking for. However, it has passed its usefulness for me. When I first downloaded about a year ago, it was the best I had ever used as as a daily scheduler. As a long range scheduler, which seems to be the path the developers are taking; there are much better ones, in my opinion. I am sad this is the direction that the developers have chosen. Now, when adding a task, it more or less behaves as a full screen pop up covering the schedule, with no way to look at the schedule for the times already entered, making you choose a time rather than 15 minutes putting it directly behind the last task as it used to do. This is totally opposite of the direction I so loved. Developers: if you change it back to KISS as in the beginning, let me know and I will happily reinstall. Also, as another comment for the autofill, I tried uninstalling hoping it would clear the history, but it didn’t. There is no way I found to clear the history or to prevent the autofill, and this was confirmed by email by developers. This last update was not the direction I needed, and was my final decision to uninstall. Just doesn’t work for me anymore.

title: Amazing & Honest, Just Needs Two Things.
body:
I love this app. I have been using it for the past few months, and I am on the Yearly Plan, soon to hop to the lifetime because I absolutely love it. It is pretty simple to use, and I love that there are time bubbles, a fun feature I tried to find in MANY other apps but unable to. I also love how customizable the app is, down to the icon, because aesthetic for my tasks is weirdly important to me. While the free version isn’t the best, that is because they want to sell the app, not your information, which is where a lot of other “free” apps get their money. And I love this new update they added to the interface, it is very nice! It is also EXTREMELY mobile friendly, with fun and unique ways to make tasks, like a time wheel and personalized icons.

   There are only really two things I would like changed, though. The cycle tracker, for whatever reason, marks the period part as one day, so it messes with its synchronization, and there is no way for me to manually fix it. It would be nice if I could manually input data into the app so it could work from there. I would also LOVE if I could share my schedule with other people on the app, so they could see what I have going on, since you can already sync it with your email. But other than those two things this app is perfect for my needs and ENTIRELY worth the money.

title: Great App! But…
body: Structured is a really amazing app. It’s helped me get motivated and stay on task, and it has an adorable design and aesthetic. My work assignments used to take a full week for me to do, because I would get into a mindset that it was really hard and that I could only do one or two tasks a day. For the hours of free time I didn’t realize I had, I would end up scrolling on my phone. But when I got structured, I could see all of my free time and schedule things in it. It lowered my screen time average significantly, and now I get my work assignments done in two days! The only issue I have is the paywall. While I understand that they need money to fund their organization, it’s blocking features that are really essential to the app. Without the repeating feature, I have to make time every day to plan out the next day, so that I can schedule out every little task individually every single day. Also, not a huge issue but some of the icons that are locked behind the paywall would be very useful, as well as the AI feature. I’m sure that the app is AMAZING if you have pro, but I don’t want to spend money every month on a PLANNER app…. Also, sometimes the schedule can feel a bit cluttered when you’re planning it out, but that’s probably just me. Overall, I would recommend getting this app, especially if you’re willing to pay! ✅

title: Few more simple fixes
body:
Structured 
- The ability to re-organize "all day" tasks and set them in an order for one event or all future events
- The ability to edit the wake up time and have it push forward all the other tasks for the day. For Example, have an option for time adjustment according to when you tap your first item so that all times adjust to the new "start," time. for people who work on call this is important since some days I don't get to bed until super late so I can't necessarily get up at the same time every day.
- The ability to tap on "all day" tasks and have them "finish" like the scheduled tasks. unless they have subtasks; then show them finished when each sub task is completed
- have the sub tasks pop up when tapping to complete a task to confirm sub tasks are completed before completely completing the main task (rather than having to tap on the task in order to see/edit the sub tasks). Also add note subtask here...as explained in the next suggestion
- add a way to add and view notes (The ability to add a note daily to a scheduled item without having to edit it. I.e. set it as an option for a task to include a note upon completion. See "Habit".) Examples are "weigh in" then the note box pops up and I enter my pounds. "exercise" I love checking off the tasks, but I have a note box below my stationary bike so I can enter the mileage and the minutes. Or for other exercises I can enter reps. For "water my plants" I can enter which ones need special attention or which ones I didn't water because they seemed too wet. Any kind of detailed note to help.  
- A section where I can review notes
- Swipe options for tasks (ie swipe left to to to add to inbox OR TO SKIP a task skipping is important --because some days I miss or need to skip but don't want to delete because I want to review what's working and what's not). 
- An option to have the schedule as a task list only  that can be re-ordered if necessary (rather than a scheduled itinerary) for people like myself who work on call and can't get up at the same time every day. 
if these could be made an option, this would be the perfect app

UPDATE:
Developer responded, but the response did not address what I was suggesting. First, "Replan" just gives you an entire list and the only options you have are to throw it in the inbox, which does absolutely nothing or swipe the other direction to market as complete.
I am looking for an option that would allow my items to stay in the list with an option to swipe to just skip for the day. 
Secondly, I went in and tried the AI as suggested; again, not what I was looking for at all. 
I still had to go in and individually accept the new time on each, and every one of the scheduled tasks which defeats the purpose of what I am suggesting. 
I'm looking for the option to be able to tap on the first item for the day and according to whatever time it is, it would automatically shift everything forward.
Seems like it might be just a simple coding command. But I'm not a developer... 
Thank you anyway for your response; maybe someday.

title: Don’t understand the hype
body: This app was recommended to me over and over for time-blocking and task management. Because there was not a free trial option, I had to pay for the app just to test the features I was interested in. (I took the scholarship option for this reason.) I didn’t want much, but the app doesn’t even really deliver on what is promised. Yes, it is a place to dump tasks. But where I wanted simple, this was way over-complicated. It claims to have a calendar, but other than the single day view, there is no functional calendar on the app. And the “time-blocking” feature really is just the string-of-pearls format shown in the previews—it’s infuriating to look at and not visually intuitive at all for me. I was also hoping to take advantage of the AI features, but they just flat out didn’t work. Either it timed out or returned with an error, or once it asked a follow-up question it wouldn’t allow me to answer. All-around just useless and frustrating for me. Added one star because it did work seamlessly with Apple reminders. But I wish I had not had to spend money on it to find out it didn’t deliver on its claims.

title: Essential for Me!
body:
I found this app to be the closest to what I was looking for in a planning app. I can sync tasks to my watch so I don’t forget what I need to do and when.

One major annoyance, however, is scheduling a time for a task. The dial to adjust the time is extra sensitive and tiny, and I find it difficult to input the proper time.

Add to this the frustration that Structured repeatedly changes the times I input. I’ll set the start time, but then when I go to set the end time, it changes the start time. Sometimes this can be fixed by making sure the amount of time spent on the task is set correctly first, but I don’t always remember to do that first and the extra step slows me down when I’m reworking a routine. Sometimes this doesn’t even fix the issue and I’m left baffled as to why Structured thinks it knows better than I do when a task should begin. 

I really want this app to work for me, but the frustration of repeatedly giving up on entering a task because it won’t allow to schedule the time correctly has me pondering if I should opt out of renewing my subscription next year.

title: These Subscription Models are Getting Out of Hand
body:
ADHD Gang: do not. This app ain’t it. The pretty planner app isn’t gonna fix you. We’ve all been there before. It’s just another app for you to sink a subscription fee into, procrastinate setting up, and forget about until it’s been taking money out of your account for months.

The full version of this app looks like it would could be helpful, but basic utility is completely locked behind a paywall. For the free version you can add a repeating wake-up/sleep time (only 1. cannot set it for certain days, only daily) and single-day non recurring tasks. You also need pro to view it as a timeline.

This is a glorified calendar. It looks pretty and is segregated from your normal calendar which was appealing to me, but at its core it is a calendar that will cost you $65 lifetime or 20 bucks a year. Back before every app and website took on a subscription model, this kind of app probably would have had something like a one time 5.99 or 9.99 download fee, then full access. You are better off just making a new (free) Google calendar for your structured routines - it might not be as visually helpful as this app but you’ll get way more utility from a free Google Calendar than you will from the free version of this app.

Not everything needs to be a subscription.

title: Best Planner App to Date
body:
I have used many different planning apps, and this one is my favorite by FAR. The other apps aren’t even close to this. I love that it has a way to put your schedule on there if you need to remember date and times, but there is also an “Inbox” which is a life saver because I can put my random to do lists in there whenever I feel overwhelmed. The whole app feels user friendly and just feels like people put a lot of thought into how the app is laid out, the features added, and overall just the appeal to using it. I struggle keeping a rigid calendar because I always forget to put things down, but this app is actually fun to use(?) idk if that’s weird but it makes me want to use it. I’m happy to see the app has gotten bigger since I first downloaded it a long time ago because I feel like it deserves it. I’ve already paid for the lifetime subscription and have zero regrets!

Also to anyone wondering about the reviews saying “you have to pay to do anything”, yes, there are some really helpful features you do need to pay for. But in my opinion it is completely worth it. The amount you pay is very reasonable for what you get, and from what I’ve read, it is a smaller company coding it, so that money goes to good use.

I have the entire day schedule (something I’ve done with other apps), but click the dot when each routine is finished and if I miss one, it doesn’t matter because the next day always feels like a fresh new day. I also really like the color customization (I have health habits scheduled in yellow, music in green, and so on). Anyway, I’ve finally found noticeable differences in my life. I highly recommend pairing this with a digital dopamine detox book and atomic habits. If you read, start your day with a bit of writing, your brain will follow through and this is the tool to make it easy to facilitate.

I, personally, didn't use it much and still don't. I'm trying to get into planning, but I wish there was an option for just a checklist for a day. The time stuff makes me confused, and I always overthink. I need to give myself 5 minutes in between, get of schedule, don't know the exact time of a class, there's a lot I need to consider when trying to plan a day with time, and I've just been looking for an app that's a checklist sorta thing where I could also plan.

Why it's a great app: It's cute, functional, and has a quite a few free features which is perfect if you don't want to pay!

Why I don't like it: You have to PAY to save custom colors for your tasks!? 🤨 That's a bit much, I can't just copy paste hex codes every time I need to change the color of a task! Again, as I stated earlier it's not for me. I will be keeping the app though cause I might use it once in a while, until I find the right app for me at least.

Edit: I have found the perfect app for me and will not be using this one! I still do recommend. If this isn’t your style, I have switched to finch as it just works better for me personally with the fun ways to customize and work together.

title: I love this app but 20 bucks for premium?
body: I decided to give this app a go in order to help me stay on top of app my daily tasks as a college student and active socializer. I purchased the one month $5 subscription in order to give it a proper go and I decided I’d commit to the steep yearly cost of $15 if I found it as helpful as I predicted. I am approaching the end of my first month today, and I honestly have had a great experience with the functionality of this app—so much so that I went to go alter my subscription to the yearly version, and was flabbergasted to see it is now marked up to $20 a year. Frankly, I am beyond disappointed. A $15 per year subscription to an elevated reminders app is already quite ambitious, but $20 is absolutely ridiculous. Unfortunately, I am caught in an ultimatum of what to do, since I truly really enjoyed the experience this app brought to my daily organization. Please let me know if any ideas, cheaper subscription plans (if there are any) or cheaper alternative apps since I just can’t justify the cost. Unfortunately disappointed.

title: Structured used to be one of my favorite apps.
body:
I’ve been using it for over a year, and it really helped me get my life together by organizing my day in a simple and visual way. When I first started, the free version had everything I needed, and I truly appreciated how accessible it was.

But over time, more and more features were locked behind a subscription. Now the app constantly pushes me to upgrade, and the limitations make it really difficult to use — even for basic planning. It’s frustrating and honestly sad to see an app that once supported me become so restricted.

I’m grateful for how much it helped me in the beginning, but the recent changes have made it hard to stick with. Unfortunately, I’ve decided to uninstall.

title: Honest Review
body:
I needed something with the deep integration to Apple Reminders, which is feeding from my work Microsoft task/to dos. This app only supports one way sync of creating task. Meaning, if they are created in reminders, it will sync to structured, however, if they were created and structured, they will not push back to reminders. The only data that seems to push back from structured to reminders is completion and dates. It would be nice to see bidirectional task creation from structured to reminders.

The UI is a little clunky when adding task in structured, it would be nice if there were quick actions that were configurable to help easily add in task. (Ex. Tomorrow at 9, and it would update the due date/alert to tomorrow at 9)

The overview of viewing all the task with the calendar data is very helpful, and love the dyslexia font was an option. I would’ve chosen this app. If the bidirectional sync of creating task was available.

title: Fits with my paper planning
body:
I’ve used time management systems for 40 years fairly religiously. They’ve evolved and changed as I’ve changed and my projects have changed. 

For me tactile paper is best. But those projects have to be reduced to daily bite-size actions. I didn’t think I’d like this because it’s a phone thing and the last thing I want is another haunt on my watch or phone. But it helps keep me on track. 

Like a bike-ride when I know the way I don’t need a map. But sometimes you do, even in familiar areas. This is like that. A map for your day in your pocket.

And I’m no slave to it. I’m guilt free if I don’t do something—push it off to another day or delete it. This might be more related to age than the program. I know from 40 years of trying you’ll die with a to-do list undone. So let that go and accept your limitations. 

So long projects and weekly goals and appointments stay on paper. But turning that into daily action is on “Structured.” Way better than a paper to-do list. 

Far fewer things fall through the cracks. I go over the day when it’s done. Push out to another time or delete the undone. Plan the next day. Watch my energy score. (You might have time but no energy to do it— that reality took me years to learn. Energy like time, is a limited resource.)

I’m older now so 18 is my energy limit. I’m getting good at estimating how much a task will take out of me. If a day has 22 energy points I can cull back on the plan or watch myself probably not get what I hoped to done. I’m fine with the outcome and take it as a learning experience and thus work on a more realistic day tomorrow. 

It’s almost like a game. Planning effectively without taking yourself too seriously. Don’t be afraid of it. Like it’ll track you as a looser cause you’ve failed at being effective before, blah blah. Let that go and have fun. If nothing else, begin to learn your limitations (because you’re human in a relentless world) and embrace them. And Play again tomorrow.

title: Incredible
body: From a personal and academic standpoint, Structured stands at what I would subjectively consider the pinnacle of task management for students, professionals, or for nonspecific users. As a student whom personally requires a degree of organization that is not intensively sophisticated, Structured offers a straightforward and intuitive platform. Other applications, Motion for example is not only overpriced for the standard user, but necessitates one to learn how to use it effectively[from a business standpoint, I am not particularly sure if this was wise]. Ultimately, this is resultant in people purchasing the software and forgetting to use it days subsequent to their costly investment. Structured on the other hand, considers that the average student might not be able to afford anything of this nature and effectively accommodates this. Further, I the simplicity and visual appeal of the UI is incredible. It’s not overstimulating and makes it relatively easy to find different organizational functions offered by the application. While I personally am unable to afford the premium as its falls outside my personal budget, the features offered here seem streamlined and could easily benefit someone who has a small amount of money to invest. On a very different note, the application is customer oriented and requests  users to purchase the premium as a way of funding further development, not necessarily to generate a profit. As a student who has a small background in front end and back end development of websites, this is incredibly selfless. I would recommend any individual, provided it falls within their budget, to purchase Structured, it is well worth it. I cant wait to see more features included in future updates.

title: Capacity & Accountability
body:
We only have 24 hours in a day. Structured allows you to plan your life in an optimized way.  

“Overlapping“ tasks  shows you where you have overextended yourself and the app also shows you where you have gaps of “free time” so you can plan accordingly.

Option to modify, duplicate and repeat tasks is beneficial.

Plus the option to sync with calendar (for me, my husband and kids) is great! 

Since I have multiple calendars that don’t all pertain to my tasks I found it helpful to create one specific calendar to sync to Structured.  This way when I have a task I want to sync on one of my other calendars, I just duplicate the task to keep it simple and clean…

It also allows me to focus and get the priority things done.

Absolutely love Structured app and can’t see living my life without it!

Thank you Structured!

title: Game Changer for Conquering ADHD
body:
What sets Structured apart from the other planners is its AI feature that works with voice to text AND it works with my Apple Watch, iPhone, and Mac — at an affordable price point!

Wake up late or have a last-minute meeting? I just tell Structured to reschedule all my planned tasks before 5. Voila, it works like magic! 

I also love that it syncs with both Google calendar and tasks, and that it’s easy to drag and drop tasks around, and dump projects and tasks in my inbox, then schedule them later. The color coding and icons also appeal to my neurodivergent brain!

What would make Structure even better? That’s easy: the ability to sync multiple Google calendars and to schedule Google calendar events in Structured (two-way synching.)

I would also like to be able to get alerts for all scheduled tasks and events on my watch even when I’m using my Mac or iPhone is in use, but I’m not entirely sure that is not a thing, or if I just haven’t figured out how to make it happen. If a developer is reading this, I’d love to know. :D

I also love how customizable it is. I can create tasks tailored to my needs and even choose colors to keep things visually appealing. It’s a simple, stress-free, and effective tool for staying on top of my schedule.

title: Useless without a subscription
body:
This app is probably great with a subscription, its cute, well designed, and I do like the visual aspect of it. However, I have ADHD and NEED reminders of tasks at least 5-30 minutes beforehand- but without the subscription this app only notifies you AT the exact time you should be starting the task. 
Additionally, the timer on the task starts whether or not you actually open the app, so often by the time I’ve prepared myself to start the task, the time window has ended. 

I’m sure I could circumvent these issues by scheduling in time to prepare for the task, but it just irritates me that I have to work around what is normally a very basic function in any planning app. 

Other apps I’ve used allow you to choose one reminder a chosen time before the task, but additional reminders require a subscription. If this was the case with Structured I would have no issue with the other features behind a paywall. 

For example you can accommodate for repeat tasks being behind a paywall by duplicating tasks and scheduling them for different days.

I completely understand that developers need to make money- but I’m simply better off using the reminders built into my phone since I do not have to pay for reminders. 

Perhaps for those without ADHD or who are already diligent planners, this would not be an issue! In that case I do recommend trying this app. It is cute and unique and I especially like the energy levels you can assign to each task.

title: Broken Reminders Sync Remains Unaddressed
body:
*IMPORTANT CAVEAT: If your app use case does not require iOS reminders sync, then disregard this review. My rating is so low because a Reminders sync issue completely crashes the app, making it unusable. I have not experienced this issue with Reminders sync disabled.*

I’m very disappointed in this app, which is overall very promising and provides a lot of functionality for a reasonable price. However, one critical issue makes the app personally unusable for me, and the developer’s suggested workaround is inefficient and inconvenient.

Reminders syncing with iOS is broken. It may work for a period of time, but there is no true solution if something goes wrong — the app just completely crashes and closes out. According to the developer’s support website, this is fixed by turning off Reminders sync.

Theoretically, according to the website, you can workaround this by enabling Reminders sync on a different device. This worked fine for a day, until my iPad’s version of the Structured app also began crashing unless I turned off the Reminders sync.

The way Structured fit into my workflow, maintaining the iOS Reminders sync let me use my HomePods and IFTTT automations to automatically add custom items both into my timeline and inbox. This functionality, when it worked, was excellent and significantly streamlined a number of steps for me in an aesthetically pleasing app.

I’m disappointed to discover that, based on Reddit reports, this has been an issue for a while. I hope that the developer issues a fix and will check back periodically, but have uninstalled the app for now as it is functionally unusable for my purposes.

title: Please Add a Share Function!
body:
Started using this planner three months ago, and I can’t overstate how user friendly this app is. The graphics and the layout are so helpful for envisioning and time-blocking your day(s). That’s said, I’ve had to part ways with this app  unfortunately, and it’s only because of this one reason: 

So, I solo travel a lot and I always make sure to share my plans with family/friends, not for the heck of it but for safety reasons; so they’re aware of my whereabouts in case anything should happen. Unfortunately, this app doesn’t have a function to do that.

Now, if this app allowed users to share their plans as a ‘view only’ or ‘allow edit’, this would be the best planner hands down— Not only would my community be able to see what I have planned for a trip but, in the case of a group getaway/vacation, it would be great so people could collaborate on plans  together- Apple Notes has this function, and it’s super helpful.

As of now (2/27/25), there’s no way for users to share plans they’ve created aside from screenshotting/ recording the app which is really not practical at all considering you have to tap through every task 1by1 in order to view the subtext/notes that you may have given each one.

When I used this app, I could easily have up to 10+ tasks in a day, some major, some minor, however for a 8-day travel, for example, screen recording myself tapping/ scrolling through each task of each day, was a giant pain and not worth the effort.

So while I would love to continue using the app, it’s just not practical for me for the way I want to use it. I guess if a user has no intent on sharing their plans/itinerary, then this is not a deal breaker. However, I think adding a share function would be beneficial regardless.

Just my opinion, I know, but I believe l this app could be instantly elevated if users could share their creations with others.

I had been looking for something like this for weeks, and after installing and erasing close to 15 apps, this one was a life saver and still helps me with everything I need to get done. You can also import from your iPhones calendar, color code the tasks, add icons and personalize everything. The AI feature is awesome! title: Complete game changer for ADHD
body:
This is truly the only tool you need if you struggle with severe executive dysfunction like me (I have ADHD, depression, anxiety, and autism). I become overwhelmed very easily and constantly drown in cycles of shutting down and bed rotting. What sets this app apart are the many thoughtful functionalities that actually WORK, as if it were created by someone who truly understands what it’s like to be dysfunctional. To name a few: 
1. The ability to seamlessly sync with iCloud, Reminders, and Calendar 
2. Separate area for thought-dumping (“oh gosh I need to do this, this, and that…”) and turning it into a deliberate action item in your schedule
3. The visual layout of the schedule. It’s simple, easy to digest at first glance, and the time-block look makes the task feel way less abstract than if the task were, say, just a bullet point
4. So many thoughtful customization options. From changing the colors and icons, repeat functionality, and more I haven’t even discovered yet.
5. The ability to label how much energy it’ll take you to complete a task. This helps to avoid burnout and space out tasks based on your own capacity. 

People like me need to “hack” our brains in a way and break down tasks into as specific, approachable, and bite-sized pieces as possible. This app allows you to do exactly that, in many ways that other apps don’t. From someone who knows what it’s like to be you, this app is different and you’ll see why.
author: Visualstudiohoe

title: The App That Helped Me to Become Who I Want To Be
body: I’ve been using this app as a tool for about a month and a half now. I have ADHD, as many people who use this do. I’ve struggled with executive dysfunction and periods of depression for years. I am a person with loads of ideas, but time management has been a problem area for me for as long as I can remember and I’ve had an extremely difficult time following through on those ideas. Your habits determine your destiny, I’ve known this to be true. I’ve tried calendar apps, paper planners, set alarms on my phone- you name it, I’ve tried it. Nothing has ever worked for me the way this app has. Everything about the simple and attractive layout, the option to choose colors for different time blocks in which you set your tasks, the cute little sound it makes when you check something off— it was designed for a low-dopamine brain. I feel motivated, I feel empowered, I feel productive. I even block out time to rest and take care of myself. I have things to look forward to every day because I spend about 15 minutes the night before planning out the next one. The structure gives me a reason to get out of bed in the morning. And because of this, I’m happier than I’ve ever been. I never knew a simple app on your phone could transform your life the way this has. To the creators of Structured, thank you.

title: This is everything I’ve ever wanted, and everything YOU will ever need
body:
I first got structured for the cross platform syncing, calendar syncing and widgets, and at the time it was probably the only app that did it coherently (it probably still is). It’s the only planner I’ve been able to use over a long period  (2.5 years going strong) of time. Everything else always ends up dropped. Not structured. 

A working example on why I’ll never drop structured—a random canvas assignment that I completely forgot about and would not have put in my planner? It’s already on structured. Someone invited me to a very important google calendar event followed by an incomprehensible email chain? The event’s already on structured. 

Structured is like magic. It takes away the large majority of the effort required in maintaining a google calendar/planner, plus you don’t have to open an app or search “_____ calendar” into the web every single time you want to see your schedule (this was always a hurdle for me). It’s already right in front of your eyes when you open your phone, when you look at your Apple Watch, When you open your laptop. It’s just *chefs kiss.

This is THE planner if you are in school, or if you work a job where everyone is seemingly giving you tasks and scheduling countless meetings out of nowhere. You will NEVER be behind because you will always know what’s next.

Plus, omg, just last week. I was like “structure is fantastic, but it would be so cool if I could still see my weekly calendar.” Then BAM I open the app today to structured 4.0. Weekly and Monthly calendar viewing. Enhanced AI to mass delete unwanted events for aren’t connect by the “repeating event” tag. It’s like they read my mind! (But they didn’t, they are just highly invested in the user experience of the app)

So for everyone who is legitimately struggling, who has bounced from notion to Evernote to obsidian to apple notes and back. I was there. Pick up structured. I guarantee you, your journey ends and begins here.

title: The best organization app I’ve ever used!!
body: I can’t say enough good things about this app! It has completely transformed the way I manage my tasks, schedule, and daily responsibilities. I’ve tried several organization apps in the past, but none have been as intuitive, reliable, and feature-rich as this one. The interface is clean and user-friendly, making it easy to navigate and customize according to my needs. I love that I can create to-do lists, set reminders, and sync everything across my devices seamlessly. Whether I’m planning my work projects, personal errands, or long-term goals, this app keeps everything in one place so I never feel overwhelmed. One of my favorite features is the ability to categorize tasks, set priority levels, and even break down larger projects into manageable steps. The reminders and notifications are super helpful, ensuring that I never miss an important deadline or appointment. Plus, the syncing is flawless—I can update my tasks on my phone and instantly see the changes on my tablet or computer. If you struggle with staying organized or just want a more efficient way to manage your time, I highly recommend this app. It’s well-designed, incredibly useful, and has made a noticeable difference in my productivity. Five stars all the way!

title: Great app, AI needs improvement
body:
I have been using this app for a couple weeks now and it has be handy to schedule my day and stay on track. I have been exploring all the features of this app and so far most of them work great but the two I have seen problems with are the AI task builder and photo upload feature. 

AI - if you are using this feature for simple tasks it’s great. But when I tried setting parameters and energy levels it didn’t recognize it and gave me poor results. Also the text prompt only gives you 500 characters so you are limited on how many tasks you can upload depending on your workload. For me I tried having it upload around five complicated tasks and it only added two of the five. 

Picture upload - this feature sounds cool but once again works for simple tasks and not for complicated/long list of items. I wrote down my task items for the day and it didn’t upload what I wrote down and spit out random items. 

The app is great but needs improvement for people who have a lot of stuff to do in the day and require more specific tasks.

title: Amazing App with Room to Grow
body:
Structured is a beautifully designed app that’s simple to use and highly effective for organizing daily tasks. I love the clean interface, visual timeline, and ease of scheduling—it’s one of the best productivity tools I’ve used.

That said, there are a few areas for improvement:

• Add shared or family calendars, and the ability to nest or display overlapping events side by side.

• Provide the option to disable checkboxes for specific events.

• Allow users to set availability for events (e.g., Tentative, Busy, Available).

• Enable selective syncing of events to Apple Calendar/Reminders (right now it only syncs one way).

• Allow editing of synced Calendar/Reminders events directly in the app.

Lastly, the Home Screen widget doesn’t load consistently, even after troubleshooting. Structured blames Apple’s background refresh, but other apps don’t have this issue.

Despite some drawbacks, Structured is an excellent app that I highly recommend. If these features and fixes were addressed, I’d give it 5 stars.

To help support them, I have a discounted yearly plan that was offered within less than 24 hours! Which for those that don’t know, is exceptional time for someone to reach back out to you! 

App itself!
Easy. Extremely EASY! It’s very simple to use and set up goals each day with sounds you can personalise. I’ve set up each day, different things on each day, and energy levels. I have lung and heart issues that make it harder for me to do tasks. Things that slow me down and make me say “you know what? I’m not doing this.” I will forfeit dishes before the day has even started. But, with energy levels on the app I can map out what I can achieve and what I can’t in a single day, in a single month, and in a single year! I can get into routines/habits that make me more conscious of my day. You can easily write things down or set reminders but if you’re like me you’ll delete them or lose the paper. Except with this app I feel a more simple, comfortable, and initiative approach. It lets me know how much time I have in between and things I can get done in that time. 

Improvements?
Overall, the app is amazing and has a beautiful layout. At the moment, I’m stuck on finding improvements because everything I personally want and like are there. I’m sure others may be more insightful with this, but if I had to pick something, maybe a seperate tab to keep appointments or plans. Let you know what it overlays and choose whether to delete or keep on that day. This is strictly coming from someone who visits doctors often, so it may not relate or matter to everyone. 

I truly appreciate all the hard work that has gone into this app! To create such a wonderful approach to “Structuring” and simplifying/maximising to achieve a specific outcome that fits everyone.

title: The app has potential but needs to be improved
body:
While the app has potential, there are several aspects that make it less user-friendly for me.

1. All-day tasks should appear in the main task list rather than as small icons at the top of the screen. These icons are easy to miss because they’re much smaller compared to the rest of the tasks.

2. The features that estimate how long a task will take and how much energy it requires feel unnecessary. Many tasks can’t be timed accurately, and the energy metric doesn’t help in planning my day.

3. It would be helpful to have a feature that shows incomplete tasks at the end of the day and asks if they should be added to the next day’s list.

4. The interface is overwhelming with too many features and buttons. A simpler, more intuitive design would make the app easier to use.

Overall, I find the app more complicated than helpful. I regret subscribing and won’t be renewing in the future.

title: Perfect for us ADD people.
body:
At first I didnt understand the inbox being such a mess and not being able to organize tasks into folders or something the way all others do, but thats the genius, it forces yo to go through the list and assign to blocks of time, thereby getting organized and accomplishing. Remind me of the REVIEW feature back in the day with Omni focus which was such a cumbersome app, they seem to have walked the design tightrope wonderfully between Things Clean-ness and their own great set up. I love the icons, it makes it almost fun setting your day up, and the integration to phone and iPad are perfect so far, I just check stuff off on my watch, updates next item. Im only on first day of trial, but impressed enough to purchase the year subscription, I think this is a keeper, Highly recommend, Put everything in it, eating, working out, appointments, so easy with widgets to stay on track, develop great habits and find welcome relaxing time. I see what 220k people are on it…it you have yet to be satisfied by a task app, this is finally the solution. 
*Developer, there is one thing I noticed, would help my workflow…if you could FIX. There is no way to add a subtask to a task without clicking the task then clicking edit task then scrolling to bottom, However, if someone set aside worktime to do a set of subtasks, they often need to add additional things as the are thought of or come up. Perhaps when you click the task and it already shows all the subtasks, you could add a + button right there or allow us to simply click a subtask and hit return right there, without the need for “edit task>scroll to bottom>click add subtask” to add another.  Hope this makes sense, I often block time for a client and need to do a list of items which they add to, this is the only thing I have encountered in your system that is counterproductive. Thank you for the future fix, I know you got it!

title: How much is your time worth?
body:
Time is money. We sell our time for money and call it work. When we use it for entertainment, we call it fun. Apps like Instagram and TikTok, although fun, can make us lose hours 15-second videos—no real progress, no productivity, and no fulfillment of goals. This app does the opposite: it gives back time.

As a woman with ADHD, managing my schedule can be both challenging and time-consuming, even though I’m good at it. This app simplifies everything, letting me just be myself. I simply list what I need to do, and it creates a schedule for me. While other apps with AI capabilities can do something similar, the best part about this one is that after it generates the schedule, I can review it, and with one click, I press “ADD ALL” and everything is instantly on my calendar for the day. Plus, I see it on my desktop, my IPad and my phone when I’m on the go. 

If this app was integrated in a Digital Touch screen wall calendar…I’d be racing for preorder. 

I invested in the lifetime membership because this app has saved me at least two hours a week—which adds up to over 100 hours a year. How much is your time worth?

title: Temporary 1 Star, read below
body:
***For now, 1 star. I can't use this on my desktop today, I only assume this is a bug induced with an update, but I can't see any new changes to my calendar on my Mac Mini which is primarily where I use it. After creating the same event three times I was able to see all three instances on my phone so they were made and all sync things are working though that shouldn't have been an issue since I made said events on my computer, not my phone. As a paid user it is effectively useless as is. After fixing this app breaking bug, I will give back a few stars, but probably only up to 3 stars until there is a not annoying way to get to the next day when at the end of a week. A 8 day dispaly at the top that is dynamic so you're never at the edge is one option as is a very obvious (in my opinion) next day arrow set just like the next week arrows. This app is old enough, popular enough, and promoted enough to not have this VERY basic feature. Scrolling to the next week and then back 6 days doesn't make it unusable, but come on....a planner/calendar app without a next day button? After bug is fixed and a next day button added, I will return to 4 stars. If things that I feel improve it enough to 5 stars I'll gladly give it (some 4 star reasons listed in original review below).***

I've really enjoyed using Structured these last few weeks. 4 stars because there are things missing that aren't really must haves for any ole' calendar app, but since this is obviously aiming to corner the App Store market for calendars, they keep it from being a 5 star experience. A partial list in no particular order:
-A weekly view
-You can add subtasks to a bigger task but can only schedule everything at once (ie, for my 'change oil' task I have subtasks of 'get supplies', 'drain and refill engine', and 'recycle old oil'; it would be great if these can be scheduled separately or the main task exists to be scheduled repeatedly until completed.)
-A way to let spouses login so they can see what you have planned throughout the day (right now I'm just sending screenshots and she can't see adjustments)
-I'd love it if I could use this feel/style for stuff that isn't necessarily on a calendar. For example, as a homeowner there is no shortage of to-dos around the house. I'd love to have a 'projects' tab or something similar where I can have big tasks/events which I'm not going to really put on my calendar but can have a list of things I need to do regarding them, what has been done so far, a place to jot notes, etc. 

Don't let this discourage you from trying Structured. There is a lot they get right from a quality, effective UI to recurring tasks that make sense in how you can customize the repeated-ness (ie, every X days, or for a weekly thing, you can say weekly on Mon, Wed, Thurs, and it will be those days every week). 

I am a paying subscriber, will probably purchase outright, and hope to see functionality improve in the coming weeks/months.

One thing I would really appreciate is a mode/version for night shift workers like myself since it can be confusing when my work-nights cross over multiple days. This takes away from the pleasing aesthetic and simplicity of the app, so I have found myself using it less since I started working on night shift. title: An ADHDer’s Dream.
body:
As a predominantly inattentive type-ADHDer, I’ve been through pretty much every planner/calendar/todo list app out there and it’s the same thing w/ every one: they either don’t work for me at all (usually do to an excessive amount of features whose usefulness is debatable) or only for a little while before I hit a wall and start searching for something else (usually the opposite, too FEW features that really take neurodivergent brains into account). 

There’s something different about Structured, though. The myriad colors/icons I can use for making the app look and feel comfortable for me, the simple and intuitive layout making inserting/planning tasks super easy to do, all of the above? I’m not sure but Structured is one of the few tools that consistently helps me get the cluttered mess known as my brain under some semblance of control and I love it dearly for that. Highly recommended.

This is so important for a variety of reasons, including if you use Calendly or another scheduling app for your business ect. Additionally, the other missing feature is that I don’t see a way to others to a task or event. And for many today, including myself, I need to be able to do that for both my personal life and work. title: Calling all procrastinators!!!
body: This app is so amazing for productivity. You get a daily timeline for activities, and create tasks that already have focus timers! I would often forget to check my notebook planner, and Calendar and Reminders and timers just didn’t do it for me. I don’t know what it is about this app, but I’m completing more tasks on time now. One feature I want (it may be Pro already, I didn’t check bc I can’t afford Pro rn 😩😭) is to be able to push back all or a selected amount of tasks. If I planned to start something at 3:00, but didn’t get home until 3:15 for some reason, then I have to edit all my tasks, or just leave the timers running and that stresses me out. One thing that I find particularly helpful about this app is that it’s given me better time estimation skills. I found that habitually late people have poor time estimation, that things take longer than they imagine it to. I schedule 30 mins to complete my math hw (this app also motivates me to try to finish b4 the timer runs out), but it ends up taking me an hour, now I know why I’m struggling in that class. Even if u end up not following your schedule, your phone will send u notifications, so I get a better idea of where my time went. Thoroughly recommend!!!!

title: Sooo close to perfect...
body:
Having been diagnosed with ADHD at 51 I started really jumping into trying to not feel like my days, weeks, months and life were constantly out of control. When I started using this app I was all in and I still like it but I have found myself moving away from it due to small things...

1. The ability to slide tasks easily and have subsequent tasks shift. Add in the ability to grab and drag task and extend or shorten the time. 

2. With that, setting and changing times require too many clicks which makes making changfes a chore which to an ADHD brain means I wont use it. 

3. If I do not complete a task have it auto shift to the next day as an all-day task that I can then assign a time to.

4. When adding tasks get rid of the suggestions. They are rarely, if ever what I want and they just clutter the interface. Give me one-click to add a task and the details using natural language input. 

Its so close and I know they are working on it. But I have started the search for something else despite having paid for a year already.

title: Game Changer for my ADD, OCD brain
body:
I've tried countless apps to help me stay organized, but Structured has been an absolute game-changer. As someone with ADD and OCD, I often struggle to keep my thoughts and tasks in order, but this app has made a significant difference in my daily life.

The intuitive design allows me to break down my day into manageable chunks, which keeps me focused and on track. The visual timeline is incredibly helpful for planning, and I love how easy it is to customize my tasks with colors, icons, and reminders.

Structured gives me the peace of mind I need to tackle each day with confidence. I can't recommend it enough for anyone looking for a tool to help manage the chaos in my mind.

title: Trying to find the best time boxing
body:
I loaded multiple planning/time boxing apps at once, and I’m trying to find the best option for my needs as a busy mom managing others’ schedules as well as my own, and for my incoming high schooler to improve on prioritization and time management. Honestly, I think this app may be in the top running, but a 3 day trial just isn’t enough. I’m not ready to commit to it for our needs yet.
One update I’d love to see for someone like me managing others’ schedules would be for some background time boxing. For example: kids’ sports physically require drop off and pick up times from me. They need to be aware of the duration for their shared calendars, but I’d love to show the middle duration in background of my personal time boxing, as I could take a conference call, grocery shop or run errands without it looking like a scheduling conflict.
I’d also love some ability to edit or delete some superfluous or conflicting events loaded from exported calendars, such as Team Snap.

I may circle back to your app in the future. I’ve liked the parts I have been able to investigate.

title: I’m so surprised
body: I’m so surprised at both the front end development off this app and by how much I utilize it. I have adhd and while people that have it have a lot of symptoms in common how it effects your day to day can vary person to person. For me I will go through several different planners over the course of the year because it takes me so long to find one that I find visually appealing and suits my lifestyle, then by the time I do find one I like its obsolete for the next year. The visuals with the dark mode on this app keep me very engaged, and I love the icon choices for tasks. I also love that I can color code between my personal stuff, medical stuff, work, school, etc…and for me being able to see the time remaining on a task and time in between one thing to the next is very helpful. Another thing I always favored a paper planner over an app for is that I tend to beat myself up if my app starts telling me I missed something or gives me a weekly rundown of so many tasks not being completed on time while on my paper planner I can just cross things off, but this app allows me to check off my list without any shaming but still providing the structure I need for my day. I also love that I can add random thoughts of things to do then insert it into my schedule when I feel ready for it. … the only additional update I wish the app had even if it was part of the subscription feature is that I’d love to be able to share my calendar with my husband, he’s like my accountability buddy and it would be nice if I could share with him what my day looks like and how much I got done, other apps offer this, like family planner apps, but the overall usage of those apps didn’t work for me like this one does.

title: Good app, a few suggestions
body:
So far I’m enjoying it, it’s simple and intuitive to use which makes it easy to get my day planned out. The clearly thoughtful, fair, and inclusive approach by the developers is also something I hugely appreciate and that will keep me using it!

A few things I’d love to see:
1. Ability to “snooze” my day—sometimes something takes longer than expected and it would be great to be able to push all upcoming tasks back by a number of minutes.
2. Way to lock tasks together so if I change a task’s time, it moves the locked task(s) with it. I like scheduling tasks in blocks but trying to shift the block earlier or later means I have to move each task individually when I’d rather just move them all simultaneously.
3. Page to see all my incomplete tasks from previous days (maybe just from the past week) to make it easy to mark them as complete or move them to a new day, so I don’t have to scroll through each day view to find things.

title: Wow! - The name says it all
body:
I recently started using the Structured app, and it has totally changed how I organize my day. This app combines a to-do list and calendar, focusing on just one day at a time, which really helps me stay on track. The best part is the colored progress bar that changes color as the day goes on. It’s satisfying to watch it fill up and keeps me motivated.

Structured is simple and easy to use, without any unnecessary features. Adding tasks is quick, and the color coding makes it easy to see what needs to be done. As someone who is ND and struggles with a million thoughts racing through my head, this is like having a personal assistant tapping me on my Apple Watch keeping me on task. It’s now an essential part of my daily routine. If you want a straightforward way to manage your day and boost your productivity, I highly recommend trying out Structured.

title: Awesome To Do List & Time Management App
body: This app is excellent.  This really deals with BOTH the To Do List AND the time management element which most To Do List apps totally lack.  I tried several apps and almost gave up.  I SERIOUSLY considered just writing a To-Do app myself as every one I used before this one pan the gambit between irritating, limited, and completely useless.  This app, though, is EXCELLENT.  I am pondering getting the Pro Version.  It offers plenty of value and no annoying ads or distractions that remove value.  The pro version gives you the ability to do much more with it.  If it becomes my daily to do list app permanently (which I am all but certain it will as it currently is and has been for months) then I will spend the money on the Pro but from what I see so far, the free version is excellent and the perks of the Pro Version look worth it.  Lifetime subscription for $49.99, which is basically what you would spend on a piece of professional software to own it for life (before EVERYTHING became a subscription model), is reasonable. I, for one, prefer buy once own forever and have no problem paying for it.  That being said, I want to try it out for a few more months before I make the plunge. Right now…an awesome to do list app that helps track both items to do and manages time, for me is worth the $50.
