title: Great for ADD! Some suggestions though.
body:
I’ma start off by saying this is perhaps the most life changing app I’ve ever gotten. I have ADD and I’ve tried to use paper planners and I never have the focus to actually get everything listed, and I hate when something changes and I have to erase and re-write it. And it leaves the “ghost” of the old event cause pencil doesn’t usually completely erase. I’m a bit OCD too 😂. 

I’m 20, and I’ve learned to just kind of accept how I am and it’s difficult some times, but I’ve made it work so far. When I told my mom I was using a planner on my phone her jaw straight up just dropped 😂 cause she knows how much trouble I’ve had with planners. 

 I also find it super tedious and boring to write the same thing for multiple days. And another thing is that when I sit down to write, I always forget what all I have to do. But with this app I can literally just whip out my phone whenever something pops in my head and add it to the inbox section. Or I can do it the moment someone tells me about it. Then when I get the chance, I can move the stuff from the inbox to wherever it should be and I know I’m not forgetting anything. 

 The app is really professional looking, and I love the color coding/icons and how you can just pick up an event and move it to a different time or even a different day. And I love how I can make repeating events so I don’t have to go and put the same thing a dozen times. I don’t have the attention for doing that manually. 

 There are a couple ideas I’ve had for the creators though. 

 • maybe there could be some sort of a detailed tutorial for all the little abilities this app has. I didn’t even know I could pick stuff up and move it around for the first week of using the app. (P.S. There was a sort-of tutorial made as events on the day I got the app, but it was pretty general to just get me started) 

 • for the inbox section, I’d totally love the ability to make folders in there. Cause I’ve been using it for stuff that doesn’t strictly have a deadline. (Which is another thing that paper planners don’t have a good system for). Like a to-do list for stuff like “oil the door hinge” which doesn’t really have a time associated with it. And It would be nice to be able to separate stuff I need to get done at the shop from stuff I need to get done at home. Whenever I get a moment I open the inbox section and find something to do. But having folders would make that a bit quicker and more organized. 

 • I’m a super visual person, so it helps me to be able to see what my week looks like as a whole. I’d say this is the biggest drawback to this app is that I can’t (or perhaps just don’t know how to cause it wasn’t in the sort-of tutorial) “zoom out” to see the entire week/month. Even if it were just to see the icons without the description, to just see the icons for each day of the week all at once would be really helpful. Then, from the month I could click the week to see just the week, and I could click a day to go back to the original view. (I have no idea how hard/realistic that would be to actually do). 

 All in all, this is a life changing app, and I super appreciate your hard work making it!

title: Fantastic app, worth the price
body:
I am someone who likes to be very organized and also has a hard time keeping track of all my plans throughout the week. My calendar app just wasn’t cutting it anymore, and I didn’t have a physical planner for school anymore. Carrying around a physical planner is a hassle anyway and it leads to me neglecting to put things in there because I forget, which is why I realized an app might work.

This popped up when I searched planner in the App Store, and I didn’t realize it was a paid app until I installed it. I did the free trial to see if it would be worth it, and I was hooked by the time the trial was over.

It works exactly how a planner app should, and even has some bonus features like AI-selected emojis for each event (you can choose your own if you want) and the ability to color code each event. You can set events to recur daily, weekly, monthly, and there’s even a spot for you to put pending plans that don’t have a day/time yet. The whole app interface is very user-friendly (and aesthetic).

I wouldn’t normally pay for such a simple app, but I use this one every single day and it really helps me keep my schedule in order. Definitely worth the $3/mo, I can see myself using this for years to come.

-I want to have a different option for the layout of the daily scheduled that looks more like iCal. The way it looks does not work well with my brain. The overlapping tasks are difficult to visualize, I don't get why overlapping tasks show up in succession to one other visually.
-I wish I could sort inbox to dos by duration, so if I am trying to plan my day I can easily find the "quick win" to dos that are less than 20 minutes in duration.

title: Review: “Structured” 🌟
body:
I recently stumbled upon the Structured app, and let me tell you, it’s a game-changer! 📅🚀

Features that Stand Out:

Intelligent AI Integration: The app’s AI component is like having a personal assistant in your pocket. It learns your habits, anticipates your needs, and suggests smart ways to optimize your time. 🤖🧠
Calendar and Planner Combo: Finally, an app that seamlessly combines both a calendar and a planner! 🗓️✍️ Whether you’re scheduling meetings, setting deadlines, or jotting down ideas, Structured has you covered.
Sleek and User-Friendly Design: The interface is clean, intuitive, and aesthetically pleasing. It’s like Marie Kondo tidied up my digital life! 🌈📲
Customizable Categories: From work tasks to personal goals, you can create custom categories and color-code them. It’s like having a rainbow of productivity! 🌈🎨
Sync Across Devices: Whether you’re on your phone, tablet, or desktop, your data stays in sync. No more frantic searches for that crucial note! 📱💻
Personal Experience:

As a fellow tech enthusiast and cybersecurity student, I appreciate how Structured respects my privacy. Plus, the AI’s suggestions have been surprisingly spot-on. It’s like having Jarvis from Iron Man whispering productivity tips in my ear! 🔐🤫

Verdict:

Structured is more than an app; it’s a digital life coach. If you want to declutter your mind, boost efficiency, and stay on top of your game, give it a whirl. Trust me, you won’t be disappointed! 🌟👏

Disclaimer: This review is based on my personal experience and enthusiasm. Your mileage may vary, but I’m confident you’ll love it too! 😊📝

One feature I wanted to use wouldn't work. And that's the "copy day" feature. I tried copying a day and the button was greyed out and said "copy 0 tasks" and I saw that above it it said something about not copying recurring tasks so I deleted the wake up and go to bed tasks, but it still didn't work. I was really disappointed because I wanted to use that feature and I tried going to the website to use the chatbot for help, but it didn't help at all. I also reset the app and went to a blank day with the morning and night tasks only with a 13hr gap in between them and tried doing it again, to no avail. 
So, I don't know why its doing that, idk how much I'll use the app because of that, but it's whatever. I'll do as much as I can. 
I wanted to use this app so I could have a schedule during the summer, since I'm still in school and have summer break and nothing going on and tend to laze around those 3 months. But since it's not working how I want, idk how well I'll be able to do it. I don't want to spend hours planning 90 days with the same schedule. And I don't want to buy pro to do recurring tasks on my own because I personally don't want to spend money on an app. 
If this problem could be fixed, that'd be great, but if not, I'll probably end up deleting the app. 
Thanks for reading 😘

title: Pretty Good, Close to Perfect
body:
Overall I dig as a planner. 

What I don’t like/ could see as an improvement:

-Option to change default reminder settings. 
Not all my tasks need three reminders to go with them. This has been the default, and I was hoping the program would learn I prefer not to have that. It does not learn it would appear to change that feature, and there’s no manual toggle to change this being the default reminder for a new task. 

-Calendar. 
In app, you navigate to the day you want to view, go to the day, and then see tasks. I would like a better heads up view. Going between week, month, next month, and three month. 

-Unfinished Tasks.
If you didn’t finish tasks, I would appreciate a recap time next day to verify if you wanted to move that tasks.. or at least move that unfinished task back in the inbox. As is, if you don’t finish a task on a day, it just stays unfinished on that day. You wouldn’t know any better unless you went back to that day and scrolled through all your tasks for that day.

title: Game-changer that needs a few changes...
body: I'm only a few days into using this, but it has already made a massive impact on my time management. It is exactly what I needed. Being able to black my day out and see where my time goes electronically and having that sync across all my devices (including widgets) just made my life so much easier.  That being said, there are a few tweak that could be made to the interface to make planning my day out less tedious. There are just too many mouse clicks involved in creating a task. The duration area could use an additional row - I often have tasks lasting more than 1.5 hours; I would like more default color options (instead of having to go to color picker so often) and the ability to customize the default colors themselves. On the main page, sliding my tasks around can sometimes be frustrating - they don't seem to "stick" where I want them to go, and the ability to extend the length of the task by clicking and dragging the top and bottom of my task bubbles would be wonderful instead of having to open the task up to adjust the duration. Lastly, the AI feature is pretty neat, however, once the list is created there is no option to edit what AI came up with without first adding the events to your day. Then you have to go tweak there. The initial page after AI creates your tasks really does need to be editable. Also an "add all" button on that page would be great. Overall, just an amazing program though. I sure hope they continue to develop and streamline some of the process though.

body:
this app is great, especially as someone who feels lost throughout the day unless i have an organized schedule! i often get distracted as i bounce from task to task but having this app helps me to stay on top of things i need to do! they send out reminders and you can design the tasks with colors and little picture icons, which i appreciate. 

the only thing i really dislike about the app are when i have overlapping tasks! it makes the schedule look really confusing. instead of overlapping tasks being side by side of each other (which would make a glance at the schedule easier to understand), overlapping tasks go on top and bottom of each other. for example, i like to study while working out. but i can’t put those tasks as overlapping tasks because it looks too confusing. like if i study from 12-4, but have an overlapping task (like working out) from 4-6, it makes the latter task seem like it starts at 6, because tasks are stacked. i would appreciate an update or option where overlapping tasks were side by side instead of on top of each other!! please. that would make this app even better! otherwise, i really enjoy and appreciate this app.

title: Great App! (+ a suggestion)
body:
I have adhd and I think the best thing about this app is how you can put things down on a schedule (and move them around and stuff) which helps when you feel really overwhelmed with tasks.

Suggestion following:
 I think an aspect that could use a little improvement would be the inbox (a place where you can put down future tasks that you need to get done along with the time it’ll take to do it.) this app would be so great if you could categorize your inbox tasks or add deadlines (and maybe starting dates as well!). I have a lot of things on my mind that I want to do “when I have time” but my list is so long (because I forget everything easily so I put it all down) that I end up just using the notes app. It would be so helpful to be able to see all of my future tasks visually in different categories. For example, you could separate tasks by whether they’re fun/east or boring/difficult. Or if you need to go out to complete it or if its related to school/hobbies/family/something else.

And with the deadlines I mean it would be helpful to see what tasks are more urgent since the deadline is closer or how many tasks you need to complete by a certain day. 

By a starting date, I mean a day after which a task could be completed. If you could add a starting date, maybe it could only appear on your tasks after that date. You could also just make a separate list somewhere and then add a reminder on the day of to add the tasks so it’s not as important as the other ones, but it would be nice. 

Anyways, it really is a good app but being able to organize your tasks so you can easily find your most important tasks/what you’re able to do at a certain moment would be sooo helpful because right now it’s just a very long list. Thanks for reading 💕

title: Best app ever
body:
Before discovering Structured, I found myself constantly jumping between different planning apps, trying to find one that could keep up with my hectic schedule while being easy to use. Structured has been a revelation. Not only does it boast a beautifully intuitive design, but its functionality has seamlessly integrated into my daily routine, making it indispensable.

What sets Structured apart for me is its perfect balance of simplicity and depth. The app allows for a detailed breakdown of my day, with time blocks for each task and event. The visual layout makes it easy to see at a glance what my day looks like, which has been a huge help in managing my time more effectively.

I've been particularly impressed with the widget feature, which gives me a quick overview of my upcoming tasks without needing to open the app. It's the little touches like this that show the developers truly understand what makes for a productive day.

Another standout feature has been the inclusivity towards students. The option for those who can't afford to pay is a thoughtful addition, ensuring that everyone has access to this fantastic tool. It's clear that the makers of Structured have put their hearts into this app, and it shows in every detail.

While I've been thoroughly satisfied with Structured, I do agree with some users who have suggested the addition of a calendar view. Being able to see my tasks and appointments on a weekly or monthly basis without scrolling would be a welcome enhancement.

In conclusion, Structured has transformed how I organize my day. Its user-friendly design, combined with powerful productivity tools, has made it my go-to planner app. I've recommended it to all my friends and colleagues, who have also found it to be a major upgrade from their previous planning methods. If you're looking for an app that can help you take control of your time and boost your productivity, look no further than Structured.

title: Love it, but…
body:
I was really excited about this app, I love the way it allows me to customize so many things. This was going to be THE app I used to plan out my day. And then I started looking into sharing my calendar with my husband so we could work around each other, and the functionality simply isn’t there. If I want to share my days schedule, he can’t do it. All the structured website says is to use a third party app. And that bothers me, if I wanted to use a third party app, I could just get another app that thought of schedule sharing within their app and call it a day. So notes to anyone who may be reading this: perfect app for the individual. Look elsewhere if you want to use this app to synchronize your schedule with other people and you want to see it all in one place.

That and it would be cool if there was the ability to shift your entire schedule down. For example, some of the plans I make for myself but don’t end up getting to them when I scheduled them out. I still want to do those tasks but trying to reschedule them in the app isn’t easy once they are on the schedule. Having the ability to re-schedule tasks to a future AVAILABLE time slot would make this app top notch.
Instead what I have to do is go back and forth between the schedule to figure out when my next available time slot is, which has caused issues with double booking.

title: Love it! But changing a task’s time frame can turn into a pain
body:
I LOVE this app! It’s been so helpful in managing my time and making sure I get everything done. However, there are a couple things I think could be improved.
    I think it would be helpful if, when you make a task longer or move it slightly later in the day all the tasks that come after it would move forward accordingly, because personally I find it frustrating when I have to go and move every single task just because I made a small time change to one.
   This of course makes me realize that there are certain tasks, such as meetings and appointment that have to stay in the same place, therefore I think it would be amazing if when you make or edit a task it has a ‘fixed’ switch you can toggle that renders it immoveable, exempting it from this forward shift.
    An alternative to this would be a selection tool where you can select several tasks at a time and move them all together. Personally I would vote for both.
    But other than this I love this app! So far it’s the best I’ve found. Keep up the good work!

title: Amazing app for organizing your daily or monthly
body:
As an avid organizer and planner, l've tried numerous productivity apps to streamline my workflow and keep my tasks organized. Among them, Structure stands out as a true gem in the realm of task management and organization.
From its sleek and intuitive interface to its robust feature set, Structure truly excels in every aspect. The app offers a seamless experience for creating, organizing, and managing tasks, projects, and deadlines. Its clean design makes it easy to navigate, while its customizable options allow users to tailor the app to their specific needs and preferences.
One of the standout features of Structure is its powerful task scheduling capabilities.
With the ability to set due dates, reminders, and recurring tasks, staying on top of deadlines has never been easier. The app's intelligent scheduling algorithms even suggest optimal times for completing tasks based on workload and priorities, helping users make the most of their time.
Another highlight of Structure is its seamless integration with other productivity tools and platforms. Whether you're using it on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac, the app syncs effortlessly across devices, ensuring that your tasks and projects are always up to date and accessible wherever you go. Plus, its compatibility with popular apps like Apple Reminders and Calendar makes it easy to incorporate into your existing workflow.
Overall, Structure is a must-have app for anyone looking to boost their productivity and take control of their schedule. With its user-friendly interface, powerful features, and seamless integration, it's the ultimate tool for organizing your life and achieving your goals. Highly recommended!

title: So close, and yet so far.
body:
Ugh! This app is so close to being fantastic. I even bought a Pro subscription for a few months, but I ultimately cancelled because of a few persistent annoyances, the biggest of which is the lack of functional flexibility and the difficulty of rescheduling events. 

This app is potentially so helpful for ND folks because it helps us visualize time, but many of us aren't that great at estimating how much time things will take. As the app is currently configured, if I go over one to-do item by five minutes, I have to individually reschedule every other thing that follows. I could just use drag and drop—and tried for a while—but it’s wonky and makes events overlap in weird ways and is generally annoying to use if you need to adjust your whole day. 

That said, this app would probably work great for those whose schedules are pretty routine and flexible, or who normally take about the same amount of time to do tasks every day. (But if you fall into that category, why not just use a standard calendar app?)

title: Life changing!
body: At the risk of sounding dramatic, this app has seriously changed my life. I have (technically undiagnosed) ADHD/ADD, and as such have  issues with getting distracted and project initiation, amongst others. I also frequently found myself feeling like I needed to be doing a task, but not remembering what it was. This app keeps my day organized, and I always feel a little bit of sense of urgency to keep up with my planner, which is exactly what I needed to stay on task. The feeling of overwhelm I previously felt is so much better and I find myself making progress on projects that I’ve been meaning to start on for literal years. Because the rest of my life is so organized, I feel like I have the time and mental bandwidth to do so much more - whether that’s being generally productive, or agreeing to plans with friends. As for the app itself - super well done and attractive with lots of customizable features. My only tiny gripe is that I wish there was a way to copy a whole day. I work shift work and on several different units, so my hours and schedule vary week to week, making it impossible to simply set recurring tasks. It appeared on the blog that there was at some point a way to do it, but it’s not clearly illustrated and the blog appears to be a bit outdated - if there is a way, I sure can’t figure it out.

title: Workarounds for Apple Watch & Monterrey bugs
body:
I really like Structured, but needed to find some work-arounds to be able to use it. 

First fix:  On MacOS Monterrey, the app always freezes on start. However, if you go to Settings —> Privacy —> Calendars —>revoke access for Structured, the. The app will stop freezing. 

Second fix: On Apple Watch, the Structured app does not display unless you upgrade the OS to the Beta Developer mode for experimental apps. Hopefully, this will work in future versions.

Otherwise, this app is wonderful. I love being able to move around blocks when I am running behind schedule. I wish it had some time tracking features like ATracker, but I’m happy to integrate the two apps for a working system. 

I am a software engineer with ADHD, so I am very particular and picky about which apps I use as the “developer tools” for my life. It takes a lot for me to adopt a new tool and integrate it into my system. Of all the apps I tried, Structured has made the cut, and become my new favorite app. Thanks Team! You are doing great work!

title: Almost great
body:
This scheduling app is pretty intuitive and good for basic scheduling. However, not sure if I’m going to continue to use it for a few reasons. #1 and most important, there is no ability to move multiple tasks at once, if you have a whole day scheduled and one tasks slips have fun going through 50 clicks to reorder your schedule. Really poor user experience for something very common and universally experienced. There should be some sort of critical path logic added, anyone familiar with a Gantt chart with be familiar with this. #2 UI is pretty wonky when rescheduling from the main schedule page good luck getting it to fall on the top of an hour. #3 reporting is non-existent, would be useful to be able to categorize your tasks so you can track how you’re spending time. They have colors but the colors don’t really do anything and you can’t customize anything about them. 

I hope they continue to improve but not sure if this will grow to anything better than a basic scheduler.

With a lot of productivity apps switching to subscription models, it’s often really hard to find the free base model really giving you a proper taste of what the app is capable of doing for your life, and most of the truly useful features are often locked behind that pay wall. I really appreciated Structured’s free app experience and I find the features locked behind the subscription are thoughtful and insightfully choices. Using the free model immediately gives me an idea of how Structured will be useful to me integrated into my life, and the fact that I don’t need to pay just to figure that out makes me INCREDIBLY happy and appreciative. I will be subscribing in the new year as soon as I get paid haha, but just wanted to leave this note so the developer knows that their thoughtfulness and care for their users is appreciated. Also your app is incredibly pretty and fun to use.

title: Need to be able to add tasks without times and time limits that repeat every day
body:
I may be missing something fundamental about the philosophy of time management this app promotes, I love the visual layout of my day, icons, reminders etc. but I find it difficult to use because I’m not a robot who takes exactly 15 minutes to have my coffee in the morning.

I have lots of things I need to do in a day and they don’t fall exactly into a little time bracket. I want to structure my tasks so that one goes after the other and I can check them off and my day moves forward. But structured forces you to schedule tasks in time slots and the day will move forward whether you’ve completed the task or not. 

It’s got no affordance to allow you to for example start being productive at 10am or 11:30am. I can’t even just select all my tasks and drag them forward through the day like you can do on a calendar app. 

I tried using the “inbox”but can’t put daily repeating tasks there. 

I tried setting them as all day events but then they lose their one after the other layout and I can’t check them off. 

I can’t reorder tasks without them “overlapping” and then I have to manually move each one. 

I think what I want is achievable if we lose the restriction to add lengths of time and set times for tasks and I can create more of a daily todo list that keeps me on track and I can reorder easily.

title: Solid but needs a few tweaks
body: This is a solid app. It does what I want in keeping track of my work itinerary. However, after using it a few days, I feel it could use a few tweaks. First,  instead of just choosing time and then answering how long, I’d like to see a simple from-to format, which it does present in certain circumstances. In other words, let me choose, via scroll selector starting time and ending time. Much quicker that way, IMO. Second, I see no way to change the date format. I like to see the date as YYYY/MM/DD instead of  MM/DD/YYYY. Ditto for the time. Much prefer 24 hour format. Finally, I’d like to see a way to export to pdf or excel. While I love the app and recognize that the developers are actively listening to feedback and working hard to add more features, at the moment I can’t give it five stars due to the lack of a few basic features that other planner apps have and would really like to see here. All in all, I highly recommend getting this app!!

title: Loving it!
body:
Thank you so much for this app! I would highly recommend it! Her is why I love this app:
1. I am an easily distracted person and with this app you can set a certain time to get things done e.g. I want to go outside for an hour, I will type in “ go outside” decide the how long I want to be outside for, and then I can change the color and icon if I absolutely want to, and then I head outside and click on the task and hit “ focus” the app will tell you how long you have left to go! It’s awesome!
2: it’s very customizable, you can change how the app looks in your App Library, and you can change the main color theme and you can customize your tasks colors and icons, and you can change the font in the actual app to dyslexic if you want to!
3: you can put notes on tasks to remember what you need to do in the task e.g. I have a task that is “ do homework” and I’ll add a note to remember what homework I’m supposed to do!
4: I love the inbox! The inbox is a place where you can put the tasks that you want to do but aren’t super important into and when you have free time, you can look in the inbox and remember what you wanted to do!
5: fairly easy to use.
6: the only bad things are that there are certain features you have to pay for e.g. repeating tasks ( bedtime and wake up not included in the pay 😉 they’re already there)
There are a few icons you could pay for if you wanted to, and then an ai assistant if you wanted help planning your day.

But over all great app! ( you don’t have to pay for the app either!)

author: The Builder....

title: EXCELLENT planner app!
body:
I have found Structured about a year or so ago, and wow… am I glad I did! As someone who enjoys planning out their day while also struggles with time management, this app has been an amazing companion. It’s really helped me as a college student, and I find myself recommending it to friends and family because it’s literally made my life 100x easier. 

The thing I like most about this app is the UX and UI design. I’m quite particular when it comes to this, and Structured definitely nails it. When it comes to usability for example, you can easily drag your tasks throughout the day in case plans change, and if you need to push back something, simply drag and drop it to the desired date and time. Plus, you can add a Structured widget and see what your current task is and how much time you have left in real time, which is incredibly convenient (it’s the first thing I see when I go to my lock and home screen). Another neat feature is the range of customization, which you gotta love. And it’s just so nice, sleek, and minimalistic: chef’s kiss 🤌 

I started off with the free plan, which already has everything you need (including the customization I mentioned earlier). But, I highly recommend getting the Pro plan. The top two things I appreciate that the plan offers are 1) a TON more icons to choose from (trust me, having a separate icon for things makes it so much more visually convenient) and 2) the recurring tasks feature, allowing me to automatically have my classes throughout the week repeated for the whole semester (and you can even assign an “end” date for this). My suggestion is to start with the free plan, feel the app out, and once you get comfortable with using it, try switching to one of the Pro plans. As a Lifetime Pro plan user, trust me… you won’t regret it. 

Of course, aside from what I’ve mentioned above, there’s a ton more features included (like the Structured AI assistant, task inbox, iCloud syncing, notifications, etc.), but there’s just too much to fit into one review (which has already gotten pretty long 😅). But that just goes to show that Structured goes above and beyond. Where other planner apps hide their best features behind their expensive plans, Structured gives everything—and more—that you need… for FREE. And aside from that, the Structured team is fantastic; they regularly update the app, listen to customer feedback, and show support for certain causes.  

TLDR; Structured is an absolute GODSEND that we don’t deserve. Try it out and see for yourself! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

title: Surprisingly Helpful
body:
I never write reviews, and I didn’t think this app would work- but it did. 

I tried out the free version, and it was fantastic and definitely can be used as is, however decided to upgrade to the paid version just so I could spend a little less time planning. I’m trying out the monthly subscription, but if this sticks long term, definitely upgrading to the lifetime subscription and LOVE that this app offers that. 

I’m the type of person that has a thousand to-do lists on both paper and in my phone notes, and I’m constantly creating reminders in my phone or events in my calendar. I’ve tried creating written schedules that go by the half hour, but I can never stick to those- but this app makes it so much easier. 

This goes for both the free and paid version: I like how I can easily move things to the next day if I didn’t get to them. I can color coordinate my activities, which helps me feel organized. And overall, having a daily calendar schedule that I can check off but also easily move around, has helped me actually get things done. 

I did end up switching to the paid version, just so I could easily add recurring tasks, but this app is definitely useful even without paying.

I tried to make the “task” ‘weekly’, with the sub tasks being what I want to get done that week, but I found I can’t make the sub tasks into a “task” that I add to the day, just the main task itself. My suggestion - make a section for today, weekly, monthly, annually, in the inbox that allows tasks to be created within those. How that helps is when I’m trying to figure out what to add to my day; I can add tasks by priority and time sensitivity.

However- if you were to schedule something weekly/daily (such as a class every X day) then you have to pay for the pro version. It isn’t expensive but I personally don’t use it because I’m broke and I like to simplify my planner. 

If you are someone that isn’t super time oriented- then I 100% recommend this app. It’s super easy to use and customize.

For the developers:
It would also be nice if we could make an account instead of syncing with iCloud. That way, we access this through a website or Windows (assuming that feature is added as well).

title: Great! ... if it would work.  Ahh, but it does
body:
Before you spend money on this app, read this.  After paying for the pro version, I installed the app on my Mac Studio, iPhone 15 Pro, and iPad Air.  The app works great on each of the devices individually, BUT the tasks will not sync across them.  After doing some research, this is a known problem.  If you plan on using this app on more than one device, do NOT buy it.  BUT WAIT...

Okay, but this app is beautiful.  It leaves all other task and calendaring apps in the dust.  The graphic display of the duration of a task or event in the timeline is what my brain needs to plan my day more effectively.  All the other apps I am aware of only show a list which makes over or under-scheduling a big problem.

The inbox feature is a bonus, and the ai planning will be a game changer for me as I learn how to use it more effectively.

Despite the syncing issues on my mac, (which I believe will be addressed because they update the app frequently) this app is intuitive and checks all the boxes for me.  

Five stars when the mac version syncs better.

body:

The one thing stopping me from hitting 5 stars is that if you have a task within another - for example, I might want to schedule in a 30 minute call during my lunch - it will pop up under my lunch with slightly overlapping edges, which absolutely kills the intuitive visuals of the app. Pleeeeeeease add this in, and it would be perfect! 

As another note, I’ve recommended this to a few of my friends who are on the Autism Spectrum like myself, and we have all found the simplicity and highly customizable notifications to be very helpful! I recommend this to all of my AuDHD-ers!

body: I’ll get straight to the point, I love this app. Firstly, it doesn’t require you to pay, sure you can to get certain features if you pay (for example making something repeat on a specific date) but it doesn’t nag you to buy it and you can easily use the app without paying. Also, if you want to pay they have a LIFETIME subscription, which most apps don’t have. I don’t pay for it but I’ve used this for over a month and I’ve been just so much better. Last year I was very unorganized because I had a play I had to practice for in school, so I basically only focused on the play (because all we did at school was practice for it) and now that it’s a new school year I needed a way to organize myself. I looked for so many different apps and out of all the ones I tried, this one is by far the best. It lets you chose your symbols for the activity (some of them are unavailable because of payed version) and set a specific time and date. Also I absolutely love how when you put a lot down on your schedule on the little free time (without an activity listed) it says “maybe take these __ minutes to rest/read a book” which I like because it has to do with my mental health and reminding me to take breaks. Overall this is just a really good app to use to schedule your day and organize yourself.

body:
The title is not an exaggeration!

I’ve been struggling with procrastination and motivation for the past three years, every little inconvenience greatly stresses me and I despise doing any little inconvenience. Work and college has been impossible to balance along with my hobbies, and I’ve been wasting days away. Many people call it “laziness” but it’s been a huge psychological hurdle for me.

However, “Structured” has made my days feel so much more productive and I actually feel like every day is an accomplishment now! Every bit of time is visualized and accounted for, which has removed so many of my burdens. This has been my most productive week in years thanks to structured! 

If there is anyone out there struggling with this along with their ADHD, I’d greatly recommend it! I wish I found it sooner.

title: Love this app, wish it had a few more qualities.
body:
Overall I think structured does a great job of helping me manage my routine, I just have some features I think could benefit. 

- Two types of tasks, simple check off tasks (what the app has now), and ‘logging’ tasks where you have to reflect or fill out a prompt to check the item (good for reflecting tasks or spiritual work.)
- Multiple inboxes that can have different names. I think have the ability to make inboxes, name them, and have task banks could be very helpful. Structured already prompts you to fill in spaces in your schedule. And I think if I was able to make a bank of task, (15 minute sweep, 2 hour laundry, etc) and label that inbox ‘common chores’ I could then repeatedly drag and drop those tasks into gaps in my schedule. This would be in addition to the regular inbox right now where if you add the task to your schedule it deletes from the inbox. 
- More custom scheduling. I would LOVE to have tasks repeat every 3rd Thursday of the month or 2nd Saturday. Being able to import celestial calendars would be amazing too. 

I recognize this is just me asking, I just thought I’d write it out in case since these functions would really bring this app from good to great for me.

title: Great app
body:
REVIEW:
I have used this app on and off over the last year and I love it. Great work! As an iOS Developer I aspire to make an app this awesome!

The app keeps me on task and helps me not get overwhelmed during my day. I know exactly what I need to be doing at any time.

BUGS:
There are a couple of bugs I have found when using the "Adjust Time" feature when setting up a new event on MacOS.

Bug #1: When manually inputting the time of an event using the "Adjust Time" feature typing in the time it can be finicky particularly when an event starts before 12:00 pm and ends after 12:00 pm.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create an event at least 15 minutes before noon (ex 10:00 am) and after 12:59 am.

2. Click on the "adjust time" button to open the "adjust time" window where you can type in the start and end time of the event.

3. Try changing the end time to 12 pm by first typing 12 into the hour selection field (ie. the last field in the end time row should say "am"rather than "pm" by default if the start time is set to a time more than an hour before 12 pm). 

You will find that the start time changes automatically because the app thinks you mean 12 am rather than 12 pm. Now you have to change the start time back to the original start time and then go to the end time and make sure to change "am" to "pm" before changing the end time to 12. This is very frustrating and I could see users giving up on the application if they don't want to take the time and energy to figure out why the app is behaving in this unexpected manner.

Bug #2: 

Steps to reproduce:

1. Start with the Structured window expanded across the entire x-axis of the desktop on MacOS. 

2. Add an event and click "adjust time".

This causes the window for adjusting the time to go off the screen. The adjust-the-time window itself is not movable so the only solution requires moving the main window of the application to the left to allow for room to see and interact with the entire adjust-the-time window.

title: Perfect
body:
This was EXACTLY what I was looking for! After just setting up one day for my tasks I immediately bought the lifetime subscription because it’s just that perfect.

I wanted a calendar-like app SEPARATE from the native one on my device that I could use to exclusively better time manage outside work (my native calendar app is filled with work appointments and trying to just “add another calendar” didn’t help me at all; I wanted them FULLY SEPARATE without having to constantly select and deselect what I’m viewing throughout the day) and no other app would do that. Every single one required syncing and if the calendar was hidden on my native app it wouldn’t show on the secondary app (what’s even the point then?).

That said if you do want syncing functionality this also has it. The major difference is this app 100% lets YOU choose how YOU want to use and integrate it.

It also just looks fantastic and has a very user friendly interface and introduction tutorial for first time users. Again, I could not be happier with this app and absolutely recommend it to anyone looking for a better calendar app and/or to do list. Also love that I can fully purchase the pro version for a one time fee instead of being forced on a monthly subscription model (something that guarantees I’ll stop using an app within a few months). Thank you to the devs so much! This app is legit perfect in every way.

title: very close to perfection
body:
User Interface and Experience:

⭕ The focus home-screen notification should be constant and not just when focus mode is enabled.
⭕ Better widget like the lock screen notification when you enable focus mode.
⭕ Focus on tasks before they actually start.
⭕ Negative timer instead of closing the focus now page so you are aware as the time passes.
⭕ Make an easily accessible button so you can just focus now on the current task without scrolling then tapping.
⭕ When you open the app, make it immediately scroll down to the current task and open the menu from where you can click focus.
⭕ Give an option when dragging and dropping tasks from day-to-day to make it all-day or the same time.
⭕ Add priority tags so when you add all-day tasks, the high priority automatically get put to the front / make inbox also have date option and show how many days left next to task name (exams, deadlines, etc).
⭕ Make folders in the top of inbox, i.e., school and work; this is for less clutter in the inbox.
⭕ Have morning/nighttime alarms built in so that Structured opens the moment you stop the alarm; unlock phone and open Structured.
⭕ Add motivational quotes / diary (basic diary) to keep people motivated to come back to Structured and plan their day.

Task Management:

⭕ Make sub-tasks more obvious instead of a tiny checkbox when not in focus mode; maybe two small red dots above the name?
⭕ Drag and drop outside of the inbox into the calendar as an event.
⭕ Notion integration w/ the calendar.
⭕ Along with being able to drag and drop tasks from inbox, being able to add them as subtasks into existing tasks would be helpful - I have a work proof every morning before school and being able to drag any task from inbox into there would be awesome.
⭕ Allow copy-pasting into subtasks for an event.
⭕ Allow images in subtasks.
⭕ For repeating tasks, show the end date.

Focus Mode and Productivity:

⭕ When in focus mode, instead of complete show a preview of the next task or of no tasks, don't show anything there because the complete button gives a sense of satisfaction that is harmful during a focus/work-heavy part of the day.
⭕ At the end of the day show a summary of what was completed and what wasn't - as a student, I have repeating tasks for school periods that I don't mark completed, so maybe keep the option of including a task in the summary on by default but off if it just adds clutter.

Widgets and Task Overview:

⭕ Improve visibility on home-screen inbox widgets; maybe make them show 4 not 2 tasks.

It integrates seamlessly with my existing calendar, which I love for appointments, and helps me see any day at a glance so I can make adjustments as needed.

title: I’ve tried a lot…
body:
I’ve tried a lot of various ways to keep myself on schedule or on task, so far this one has been very helpful! Will it be helpful for those who don’t enjoy keeping lists? Maybe! There are other features that may help you.

For me, though, this app is like combining the Reminders, Notes, and Clock (alarms) apps that I already use to maintain a semblance of structure, plus any other 3rd party app I’ve been struggling to keep up with, all into one easy place. Plus it’s pretty, they support LGBT people, they don’t require you create an account, and they value all of their customers by offering price points that makes their pro version accessible to anyone who may need it. More over they offer a life-time purchase option if you despise the subscription model most apps require, and I don’t mean some steep $140 price tag. Their life-time version is $40, which genuinely feels reasonable.

Can’t wait to see how they continue to improve into the future, but even if they finished here and focused on maintaining the app I think they’ve created something they should be proud of. 👍

author: SomeoneNameBob

title: Great deal for a great app
body:
Tried a bunch of planner apps, and lots of experiments with my ideal scheduling lifestyle… and here I am loving this lovely little app.

It’s easy, I dare say ‘fun’. Intuitive.
Enough features to create a daily/weekly/monthly schedule.

I like that it focuses on a day at a time but lets your schedule recurring tasks whenever.

I LOVE the sidebar style inbox where I can drop tasks full of lists of things I do often but not in a set time or mixed into a window of time which I have set for a specific activity - I like to do minitasks during my breaks, so this feature proves invaluable to me - I can clear my head but know what I need to do at a glance.

The visual style and feel of the app is charming. Really relaxing which fits my need for a relaxed atmosphere.

This app can do a lot of lifting in a way that doesn’t force you to see your to-do piles. Has a very minimalist feeling but with warmth and softness built in to the interface design. Much better than a lot of the hard edged blocks. The loads of colors is a big plus.

And it sets the times properly. Even when you cross over the midnight hour - it works.

I love it. 5 stars.
I tested this app all day before I hit the rediculously well priced pro upgrade. Thank you for that.

I can see myself using this app for the long haul. It’s so easygoing yet marvelously functional.

A really well thought out app!
Great job!

The huge variety of icons available to mark events, the option of using different colors for different things, the indicators of times when you don't have anything scheduled, these are all great. Really just excellent, I'm glad I bought it, and after using it for more than 6 months can say it's a bargain.

title: Great but has issues
body:
First of all I love this app and purchased the lifetime subscription, I’ve used it for a few years now and it is useful but I have a couple issues. 1 - I can not get my Apple Watch app to sync no matter what I try. I have followed the trouble shooting guide but it is stuck in sync mode. 2 - I wish overlapping tasks weren’t shown above or below but side by side. Any overlapping tasks make the app annoying to use and unfortunately I have a lot of scheduled things that overlap. It feels like half the screen is just dead space. The task hourglass effect on the day view  is awesome but really only if there’s no overlap. This also makes planning events hard since everything gets spaced out so much with no real organizing. 3 - A week view is desperately needed. Your only option is to look at every day individually. 4 - the physical lengths of tasks in the day view are off. An 8 hour task is barely longer in length than a 2 hour task. I love the hourglass effect but this doesn’t work for it. 5 - you can’t update icons for recurring events imported from your calendar, they almost all have the calendar icon by default. 

If I could fix these issues the app would be seriously perfect. The ability to assign hex codes to not just the tasks but the entire UI is such an amazing feature and this app has the best widgets and focus but I unfortunately have to use other apps for my scheduling/task management needs.

title: Simple to use but powerful great for visual folks!
body:
I started using this to help w ADHD post medication. I need something visual.
It's helped me plan my day the night before as opposed to being overwhelmed in the morning. 
It's also helped me to be *realistic* about what I can accomplish. (Give yourself buffer and downtime!)

It's the kind of app that's simple and intuitive, not overwhelming.  I keep finding new features I slowly integrate. I just discovered "focus mode" by accident! (I have paid. It's so cheap, just go for it for a month) the task box can be used to store skipped tasks or as a mind dump. 

The widget works perfect. Works w my watch, too. 

I see a large upgrade is in the works. I would like to see a way to pause or shift the whole itinerary if I get behind because life/ADHD happens. Or group chunks of tasks that are dependent on each other. The default peach color is kind of meh. Would like to choose white or black icon colors. Can be slow to open, but you won't need to if you stay on track (widget). Lastly, when I have sub tasks, I need a really noticeable visual reminder bc it's not obvious. 
Don't let any of this put you off. I rarely take to any time management app so quickly. TRY IT!

title: Clean + Helpful
body:
The app, when first opened, can look a bit cluttered (especially if you have a small screen like I do). But as you begin to use it, it becomes incredibly intuitive and is actually really efficient~ you can create small tasks in seconds, and with notifications on, you may find yourself actually stopping your procrastination for once (if you’re naturally productive, you don’t need this!). That said, I do have a few issues with the app. 

First: I have an iPhone 8, which has a really small screen. Because of this, the normal “Full” interface doesn’t actually fit on the screen (the times and some of the dates that are supposed to be in the margins didn’t show). So it would be amazing if you could make the app adaptive so that it fits on small screens too (I know that this is a bit of a niche issue)

Second: I NEED to be able to make recurring tasks. This is seriously a dealbreaker for me, because many of the tasks I need reminding of are ones I do on a daily basis, meaning that unless I can make them recurring, I will have to create a new task every single day for the exact same thing. Very frustrating. Obviously, I understand that some things need to be “pro” features, but I would greatly appreciate to just have one of the recurring features available (either daily, weekly, or monthly). 

Thank you so much!!!

title: Perfect for the Structured Among Us
body:
I have been looking for this app all of my digital life. If you are a freakishly organized person, you need it too. Here’s why: 
1. You can literally plan out every second of your day, one task at a time. I add in drive time between errands, work, etc, which helps me to see what time I will actually get home. I add in making dinner, getting dressed, etc. By the end of my list of tasks, I can see how much free time I will ACTUALLY have each day. All the little things add up and you never have what you think you will. This may sound excessive, but that gets into…
2. You can copy tasks to another day, and even better, set them to repeat as often as you need to. For example, I know it will take me 30 minutes to get dressed in the morning, so I have that set to repeat every day. I can scoot my getting ready time to whatever time it will be, but it will pop up for each day. 
3. You can set the app to sync up with the reminders and calendar apps on your iPhone. So as long as you’re putting all your appointments in your calendar, they will automatically pop up in Structured. That is amazing and very helpful. 
4. There is a section for tasks you need to get done at some point, but don’t know when. When I see I have an extra 30 minutes in my day, I can just pop in one of those tasks with one tap. So easy. 
5. I guess it’s not important, but all the color and icon choices are a plus for me. It makes it fun to add icons to tasks and keep them color coordinated. But I am a nerd. To each his own. 
There are more things, but this review is getting long. Try it out and see what you think!
author: Lillieflowers

title: Amazing if you need someone to tell you when to start/stop things
body:
I live with treatment resistant bipolar I, and because it is treatment resistant I’ve had to make significant lifestyle changes to help manage it and prevent mood episodes. One of these changes (and one of the most important ones at that) is by implementing and sticking to strict routines. Mood episodes are often caused by variances in your sleep/wake cycle, so that’s part of it- but having a strict routine also alerts other people near you when something is wrong because it’s much easier to tell when you’re not okay/starting an episode. 

One issue though, is that I also have ADHD and I can’t take anything for it because the medication triggers mania for me. Time constantly gets away from me and I end up sitting in one spot for 10 hours and yet not even finding time for mundane things like brushing my teeth- for a long time I’ve felt like I’ve just been going in circles- I get nothing done all day, so I can’t sleep at correct times because there are things I HAVE to get done, mood episode triggers, interventions cause even more disruption to normal living, hospital staff establishes routines, get better, rinse and repeat. 

My therapist recently recommended using an app or alarms to track my day and keep things moving along- I looked at a lot but so many are very expensive and don’t even offer much. I downloaded this one because it has a lifetime purchase option of $30 or a month at $3 (or year at $10)- this is perfectly reasonable. While I don’t think apps should be free because they take time, energy and money to make (and developers deserve to be paid for this)- I also didn’t want to pay a lot for something that may not even work for me; my bipolar already costs me enough as is. 

I didn’t try the free features, so I can’t speak to those- but I love this app. I didn’t realize how much having something remind me to to start/stop even just basic little things would make such a difference. I’ve only been using it for a month, but I’ve gotten so much stuff done that I’m actually impressed with myself. I’m fully caught up at work, my house is clean, I’m showering and brushing my teeth at correct intervals, I’m even reading again and taking nice walks with my dog. I always thought I was just incredibly lazy and would beat myself up over it even while my therapist tried to explain that I just lacked a proper sense of passing time and I’m finally starting to understand that. You can get so much stuff done a day if you just plan it and stick to it! I used to make decisions like “should I brush my teeth, shower, take a walk or get caught up on work today?” Like I could only do one task at all on any given day. I haven’t felt so proud of myself in so long, even if it’s just for functional like a normal human being- but this app has honestly been a lifesaver for me. 

I also love the calendar sync features because I can sync all my work meetings and personal obligations right into my schedule. The only thing I currently wish the app could do is allow me to just swap two tasks. It would also be nice if there was a type of report you could see that tracked things you didn’t click off so you can start to understand why you might have been missing stuff (maybe two tasks need to be spread out- maybe one takes longer than you think, etc). 

But now I just do whatever my Apple Watch says I should be doing, whether it’s reading, working, eating, showering or just relaxing- and my life is actually looking a lot brighter.

title: The best planner and widgets
body: This is by far the best planner app I’ve found. I’ve been using a routine app and a to-do app, and I schedule them in Structured to have a clear timeline of my day. The widget is the absolute best. I’d really like the see the ability to “overlap tasks”. Imagine I have breaks during work and need to do errands, it would awesome if I could place these errands during my scheduled work block and have it automatically cut that section of time from the work block and also refill that time if I need to delete the errand. Usually the user would have to manually create and organize these instances. A way to build on this could be to distinguish between tasks that have a set deadline and tasks that have an amount-of-time requirement. If the underlying block has a deadline, an overlapping block will cut out the time necessary from the underlying block. If an underlying block has an amount-of-time needed, an overlapping block will split the underlying task where the new task begins and push the remainder of the underlying task forward instead of just cutting out the time.

Editing tasks is also a huge hassle and not user friendly. But if I add my tasks to reminders, like I said they don’t always show up. I wish I could be refunded. This app would be fine free. title: Great Idea, Buggy Mac App
body:
The integration with Apple Reminders is great, and the time-blocking functionality is incredibly useful.

However, I've tried integrating this into my daily workflow, and the Mac app has too many bugs for a daily driver app. Here are just a few:
* It's impossible to adjust the duration precisely, especially in the minutes tab.
* "Hiding" reminders from the daily schedule does not work
* Recurring tasks don't auto-populate until they're complete on the previous day
* And a handful of others

Once these are ironed out, I can easily see this as a five-star app. But in its current iteration, it's just too buggy to be reliable. Which is unfortunate. The necessary improvements should be relatively simple to make.

I'd advise the developers to stress-test the app on all its different platforms, make a list of all the bugs to iron out, and knock them out one-by-one. This would make a much bigger difference than adding new, semi-useless features that 95% of users won't take advantage of.

title: Could use some (actually useful) changes
body: I have structured pro and have been using it for a couple months. For the most part, it gets the job done. It is a relatively cheap alternative to many other scheduling apps on the market. However I have a few complaints. The largest complaint pertains to the new AI update. This app is missing some key features, like auto creating events when you type (most other paid calendar apps on the market have this feature). They have been teasing new features and updates that seemed like they would actually be useful. Instead, they launched this new AI- it is essentially Chat GPT but significantly worse. If i want to use it, i have to type in my day and then wait several minutes for it to work. I havent been patient enough to even see how long it would take because i usually give up after 3-5 minutes. If you dont want to wait and go back to the home page, it stops loading and cancels whatever you were doing. So instead of creating an actually useful update, they just hopped onto the AI train but in a really poorly designed and not-thought out way. It would be easier, faster, and more effective to just go onto chat pgpt yourself and type it all out there. I know that every company wants an AI chat bot right now, but if you are just basically going to add an link to a preexisting chat bot but with even less functionality, it is not an update even worth releasing. G-cal integration (outside of ical), a web based app to use on the go, better UI are all things that need actual updating. Do not let the “AI” banner talk you into buying the paid version, as the free version of chat gpt works way better. Please work on things that people have been actually asking for.

title: I had my most successful college semester because of Structured
body: I cannot emphasize enough how instrumental this app was to my most recent semester of college. My first two years were rough. I struggled with mental health and was doing very poorly academicaly ( i couldn't get an A to save my life). I was diagnosed with ADHD in my second year, I took a semester off, and when i returned, structured made the biggest difference in managing my time. The features helped me create realistic timetables and challenged me to complete tasks within the time i alotted for it. everytime i crossed off a task, especially if i completed it in less time than i anticipated, i was easily able to adjust my plan and give myself more downtime. It was also useful for deadlines because i was able to put hw, tests, quizzes and the like in as an all-day task so I would know what was due and when.

If you want you can also make it every 2 or 3 days. My problem with this is I feel like you should be able to make certain tasks only for weekdays or weekends like for school or work. Other than adding more icons and improving the daily/weekly system Structured is an amazing daily planner app and I would really recommend getting it.

Second when i did get the navigation down and found the feature i was looking for (repeat: daily weekly monthly) it was considered a paid feature. While I’m on the subject thirdly every time I did do a task, it seem like the app took every opportunity to remind me to buy the full version. Maybe this was why they pitch it early and frequently so you don’t notice. Needless to say, I spent more time fighting the actual app than utilizing it in my actual life. 

I do like the inbox feature! Me being on the ADHD spectrum I find that being able to dump all my ideas into a basket, and then find time throughout the day to get certain task done is a huge benefit that not many other apps offered. Maybe if the interface wasn’t so cluttered and it wasn’t paywalling essential features I would consider purchasing the full version in a one time unlock all sorta situation.

title: Excellent App, but One Feature Missing
body:
I will start by saying that I NEVER leave reviews for anything. I felt compelled to write this one because I love this app, but there is one feature missing that I would love to see added in the future. 

First, the reasons why I love it. I am a graduate student that struggles to manage time well, and this app allows you to "focus" during scheduled events. For example, if you block out two hours to study, the focus feature allows you to display the event on the entire screen with a countdown timer. I also love that you can easily create checklists within scheduled events. Lastly, Structured easily syncs with Google calendar, which I use as well. 

Now to where the app is lacking. There is a simplified monthly calendar view and, of course, a detailed daily view. I wish so badly that Structured would add a weekly view. This view helps me manage work, school and personal time easily. With this one additional view, I think this app would be PERFECT.
author: CharlieStudies

title: Great app, just a few more features
body:
Great app for showing people how much time they actually have available, however I’d expect a few more features. I went ahead and got the Lifetime membership for the very big feature this app offers which is to connect to your IOS calendar and reminders so everything is in one place. I can already see myself getting lost and trying to find the current day I am. There is no “Today” button from what I can see. The calendar view is more of a navigation tool and doesn’t give you any information about the day your clicking on until you arrive there. Adding a more intuitive notes section would be very good as well so I can easily make a note of why I didn’t complete the task when it was due. I feel as if it could do more with widgets as well, only 3 selections is fairly limiting.

The app is great for people who have adhd. As I said earlier, it really helps show you how much time is available for you. When I installed this app and looked at my work days and days where I had appointments I realized I could get so much. Time blindness is real and this is a perfect remedy.

title: Cool idea, very limited.
body:
As a 3rd shift worker, structuring my calendar around when I wake and sleep would have been incredible. Unfortunately, this app does not allow:

1.) concurrent events
I use time blocking, and having a visual chunk of the day with little events within is very helpful to me. Especially having a “work” block and having alerts for critical calls or tasks throughout that window. It allows you to pick any time, but turns into a visual mess immediately. 

2.) reoccurring tasks within the inbox
Reoccurring events are possible but not tasks. You have to recreate them all from scratch each time. 

Also, when you start to make an event it shows “suggestions” below. Those edit the previous events by default and are not templates. I messed up multiple events thinking they were templates like in Apple Calendar.

title: READ THIS BEFORE GETTING THIS APP!!!!! 🙏
body: Whenever I am about to download an app I always try to read the reviews to see if what I am getting is really worth the storage space. I got this app after reading the positive reviews and was most certainly impressed. This is an honest review free of any bias. Lately, it seems that all of the apps out there are after money, constantly asking for ridiculous amounts of money just for you to be able to use their “free” app. On this app their is a daily planning workspace that is completely free of charge, with most things on thee space free of charge as well. I do wish, however, that you were able to choose different wake-up times depending on the day. Almost all of the symbols (used as a picture for your event) are free, which I really love, and you are freely able to change the color of said symbols. There are unlimited events in a day, so you could make a new one every minute if liked. But beware, this app does NOT offer free monthly planning. I’m order to have access to the monthly calendar you do have to pay a fee. It is not large, about 4p10 dollars a year I believe, and it does have a lifetime payment of about $30, which I am always very fond of. Of course, I always wish that every app was completely free, hence the four stars, but it is what is is. Overall I really enjoy using this app, and I may even end up paying the lifetime fee in the long run. It is probably the best app out there for busy schedules.

title: Lots of potential but needs a LOT of follow through by devs
body:
The performance is unpredictably awful.
The app crashes randomly.
Some events and reminders are sync'd multiple times.
Scrolling has lag
Clicking to check off an event has a significant pause before the event is checked

All to say that this is more of an alpha release than a production ready product.  Great concept. Needs a LOT of attention to details. 

UX is more than just appearance. It's how the app feels. Lag and crashes feel bad. 

Update 2023-04-21: dev responded
Dev: Assking if I had updated all of my Apple devices? 
Me: Yes, I keep all of my devices on the latest OS version at all times. All of my devices are current.
Dev: Duplicate reminders can come from enabling sync on multiple devices
Me: This sounds like a bug. Apple must have a facility for detecting this for cross-product apps? Can't this configuration be stored in iCloud as part of the sync to prevent allowing users from accidentally putting the app into a bad state?

I'll reiterate: it's a great concept. I paid for a lifetime subscription! However, there are an enormous amount of rough edges! 

I wish the dev success, hope that they can scale their business, and fix these bugs faster. I'm nervous that this application has been around for 3 years already and still have so many performance and crashing issues.

title: Love! Have some suggestions
body:
I was feeling overwhelmed with balancing studies, my freelancing and personal life and was looking for a really flexible daily planner that could help me be more productive during the day. This definitely helped me and I’ve been using it religiously for the past days. I also love that I can access it on my apple watch.

I do have some suggestions that help increase the productivity of the app. It would be helpful if we could somehow include deadlines or create a larger task that we can then split up into smaller work increments. For example, if I have to finish a project that takes around 8 hours total, I currently have to create four different tasks to address that project. Would be cool if I could just add the project into my inbox and distribute the hours into my days from there. 

It would also be helpful if the app suggested when to add tasks from the inbox or made those more visible so I could remember to place them. 

Overall great app but can see how little changes could increase how effective it is!

title: Great tool for lifestyle management
body:
2023-03-28
Update 3.0.6 just dropped adding, “Drag-and-drop” for tasks. This update is great (no bugs experienced on my end).

Drag-and-drop provides a bunch of flexibility that covers other things I’d like to do. Initially I was hoping for a way to chain tasks (so when I move my 6am, the ‘chained’ 8am moves too); but as a programmer myself I know the horror dependencies can cause in any program. The ease of drag-and-drop let’s me rearrange my tasks quickly and easily; giving me the quick customization needed to leverage this app as the core intraday planning tool that I want it to be!

2023-03-24
To balance the various tasks across my responsibilities to: my partner, my employer, my peers, and myself, I’ve built an all-encompassing system of notebooks. The main weakness of this system was a lack of synchronization; I can’t carry all 5 notebooks everywhere I go (comfortably; albeit I did try for awhile). This app has been a great plug to capture the day-to-day tasks that come up across these various life responsibilities. A major advantage is being able to setup iterative tasks with longer periods (like ‘Apply fertilizer’ or ‘Dentist checkup’) that tend to slip off both day-to-day and long-term task management systems. The more I leverage this tool, the better it helps. I’ve yet to reintegrate it into a calendar application (I use Microsoft products heavily) but I’m looking forward to leveraging that feature as well! 

 Finally, I know it’s difficult for app developers to compete in a subscription-heavy market, but having lifetime membership options is very refreshing. I would definitely pay a higher lifetime membership cost to help offset the difference against subscription options, because I’m very much over subscription services. 

 Love the product; hope my review helps others jump in and find value with this product as well!

title: Not Synching with AW
body: I love this app, so much so that I bought a lifetime pro membership. My primary reason for choosing it over other ADD apps was it’s compatibility with my Apple Watch. It has now stopped synching not only to the watch, but to my three iPads as well. It works just fine on my phone and MacBook. I followed everything in the Help section, yes iCloud is turned on everywhere, and I have nearly 2T of FREE space. I have wasted hours trying everything - repeatedly deleting/reinstalling the app, etc. In the app, it is showing “synching,” on the watch it shows “synching” with “most recently synched” and the time is usually about 1 minute prior to when I’m checking it - yet it is not synching. On the AW, the daily schedule does not show at all, the complication has disappeared. BUT THE REAL REASON FOR THE ONE STAR REVIEW IS THE TOTAL LACK OF CUSTOMER SERVICE. I contacted them and was met with an automated email response telling me to check the help section (of course I already did), and that if I still needed help (obviously I do), then respond to the email. So I did. NO RESPONSE WHATSOEVER. Also troubling, the “help” section basically states that “oh well, I can’t control Apple.” Ok, well see, that’s a problem. You sold a product, touting a feature. You don’t get to turn around and blame the lack of functionality of that feature on a third party. You have an obligation to REMEDY THE PROBLEM, not throw your hands in the air. My takeaway here is not to pay for lifetime subscriptions. Lesson learned. Leo, I WILL CONTINUE TO LEAVE ONE STAR REVIEWS UNTIL I GET A VALID RESPONSE FROM CUSTOMERSERVICE! When and if I do get a valid response, I will replace this review with a more charitable one.

title: Makes a Physical Planner Obsolete
body: Immediately after installing this app, I knew that this was going to help me IMMENSELY in my everyday life. I'm a college student and am currently working full-time, so I lead a very busy life which can oftentimes spiral completely out of control and I end up losing sight of responsibilities in my life that are not obligatory. This helps keep that in check, and does a much better job than a physical planner, I'll add. I hate physical planners because they take up space in your bag and are just one extra thing you've gotta remember to tend to each day. Odds are, you already use your computer every day and if you're a college student who uses a laptop like myself, you also happen to take it with you everywhere. It's so easy to remember to use this planner every day and it has some incredible features that a physical planner could never offer. For instance, you can set recurring tasks. I have recurring tasks for the time I wake up and go to sleep on the weekends and weekdays, as well as my work and school schedule. Each task can be assigned a neat little icon and a specific color, in addition to having a field for a description of the task itself. What I find the nicest is that the whole design of the app works wonderfully with the appearance of MacOS, which is something most other digital planners fall short with. Of course, some of what I mentioned does require that you purchase their premium features but it shouldn't get you down, it's quite cheap. Only $10 annually, which is about how much you'd spend each year on physical planners. Alternatively, you can spend $30 and have lifetime access to their premium features. Even without these features, the app is still incredible and is a must-have for anyone who values keeping their life in order.

title: best scheduling app & a few ideas!
body: hi! just wanted to say i appreciate this app so much! i bough premium lifetime and have it on both my imac and my iphone. at first i didn’t use it much because i was intimidated by having to plan my hourly schedule with adhd. since i bought it though, they’ve updated the app quite a few times and i now use it daily! (especially since adding being able to drag tasks instead of putting exact times.) structured has made it very accessible, and i am so grateful for them offering affordable lifetime membership as another option as opposed to other apps that only have subscription based memberships. i also use other apps by this developer such as their budgeting app and habit tracker which are both really useful to me. i have a few ideas and i hope you’ll consider adding them! one thing i would love to see is being able to have an option to create different preset schedules for specific types of days (ex. day off, work, day out, etc.) instead of having to be tied directly to your calendar if that makes sense. i love the reoccurring task option, but it can be difficult to move tasks around when there’s a pop up asking if you want to move all/only future/or just that task each time you have to swap some things around. having premade schedules/presets you could swap in would be fantastic! it would also be nice if you could schedule these presets more in order of activity/task and less specific hour:minute times so that you could adjust them easier when you apply them. or if you could have some sort of place to organize your tasks for the day without having to clear a day of already reoccurring tasks. kinda like inbox but the tasks won’t disappear when you add them. you can just plan a whole day and then add it to a list of saved schedules. hopefully that made sense. some other things that i would love to see someday!!:-the app could take a list of tasks and randomly schedule based on priority (this would be super useful imo) -compatibility with alexa to add tasks/remind/check off -option to make sub tasks more noticeable/visible -more icons/customization (great selection already though!) -more connectivity to the other apps from same developer (budget app, habit tracker, etc.) -i’m not sure why but the interface has been a bit laggy lately when trying to check off tasks. it’s not so bad, but it occasionally freezes or does something multiple times but delayed some things i love: -can drag tasks to move them around -pride icons!! queer friendly :) -the widgets are highly customizable and very useful! -suggestions for tasks and filling schedule make it less intimidating -frequent updates/devs listen to their user’s feedback and add new features -lifetime memberships instead of forced subscription layout (i believe on their other apps they also allow very low income users to request subscriptions if they cannot afford it but i might be wrong) anyway, for anyone debating on getting this app, it’s very worth it.

Cons: The app fell short on advertising that it could be a calendar too. Once integrated with your other systems, you can't use it to move anything that was pulled in. So, you still have to keep your other calendar apps handy. It also wouldn't let you see any of the true functionality until you paid for it. There should at least be a 7 day trial so that people can really see what this is capable of. I got asked for a review 5 minutes into using it, not a great start. It gave me warnings that there were things that were overlapping, but gave me no easy way to resolve this issue.

Since I like to test systems, I went ahead and paid the lifetime. So maybe wtih more development it will actually be worth using. As of right now, it's not useful if I have to keep all of my other apps just to use this one.

body: As someone who’s suffered with managing my ADHD symptoms my entire life, I enjoyed seeing how intuitive this app is.
